post.description:
Send a new message.

Supports 3 resolution modes:

**Mode 1: conversation_id only** (reply to existing conversation)
- Just provide `conversation_id` and `text`. The recipient is auto-resolved
  from the conversation's contact method or last inbound message.

**Mode 2: contact_method_id** (cleanest, resolves everything)
- Provide `contact_method_id` and `text`. The `to`, `channel_id`, and `contact_id`
  are all resolved from the contact method record automatically.

**Mode 3: contact_id + optional to + channel_id** (explicit)
- Provide `contact_id` (and optionally `to` and `channel_id`). The conversation is
  auto-resolved from the contact. A contact_method is auto-created if needed.

All modes are backward compatible. Existing requests with `to` + `conversation_id`
continue to work.

**Required Scopes:** `messages:create`

mode1_conversation_only.description: Send a message to an existing conversation. The recipient is auto-resolved from the conversation's contact method or last inbound message.

value.text: Hello! Your order #12345 has been shipped.

mode2_contact_method.description: Send a message using a contact method ID. Everything (to, channel_id, contact_id) is resolved automatically.

value.text: Your appointment is confirmed for tomorrow.

mode3_contact_auto_resolve.description: Send a message to a contact. The conversation and channel are auto-resolved. A contact_method is auto-created if needed.

value.text: Welcome! How can we help you today?

backward_compatible.description: Existing format with explicit recipient and conversation ID still works.

value.text: Hello! Your order #12345 has been shipped.

image_with_contact.description: Send an image to a contact with attachments and metadata.

get.description:
List messages for a conversation, or tenant-wide by status/direction.

**Conversation mode** (`conversation_id` given): unchanged. Cursor or page pagination.

**Tenant-wide mode** (no `conversation_id`, but `status` and/or `direction` given):
returns messages across all conversations of the tenant, newest first
(`created_at` desc), page/page_size pagination only. Example:
`GET /messages?status=failed&direction=outbound&page_size=3` lists recent failed
outbound messages. Limited to the last 30 days unless `created_after` is given.
Each item is the normal message object (incl. `error_message`, `conversation_id`,
`contact_id`, `channel_id`, `platform`); `contact_id`/`channel_id` fall back to the
conversation's values when the message row has none.

Supports two pagination modes in conversation mode:

Supports two pagination modes:
1. **Page-based (standard)**: Use `page` and `page_size` parameters
2. **Cursor pagination (recommended for large datasets)**: Use `cursor` parameter for O(1)
   performance regardless of page number. Returns `next_cursor` in response.

For tables with billions of rows, always use cursor pagination.

**Required Scopes:** `messages:read`

post.description:
Create an internal note on a conversation.

Internal notes are visible only to agents and are **never** sent to
the customer. They appear in the conversation timeline styled
differently from regular messages.

Supports @mentions: pass `mentioned_user_ids` to notify other team
members. Each mentioned user receives an in-app notification with a
deep link to the conversation.

Optional `assign_to_user_id` also assigns the conversation. That needs
the same permission as the assign endpoint: `conversations:update`
(403 otherwise, and the note is not created), the cross-agent reassign
rule, and an active workspace member as assignee (400 otherwise).

**Required Scopes:** `messages:create` (+ `conversations:update` when
`assign_to_user_id` changes the assignee)

post.description:
Send an interactive message with buttons or list menu.

Interactive messages provide rich UI elements for user engagement.
Currently supported on **WhatsApp only**. Other platforms will return
an error with guidance on supported alternatives.

## Message Types

### Buttons (`type: "buttons"`)
- Maximum 3 reply buttons
- Each button has an `id` (returned when clicked) and `title` (max 20 chars)
- Great for simple choices like "Yes/No", "Accept/Decline"

### List Menu (`type: "list"`)
- Up to 10 sections with rows
- Each row has `id`, `title` (max 24 chars), and optional `description`
- Maximum 10 total rows across all sections
- Great for menus, product listings, options

### Request Contact Info (`type: "request_contact_info"`)
- A single button asking the user to share their own WhatsApp phone number
- Only `body` is used — the button label is fixed by WhatsApp and shown in
  the recipient's app language, so `buttons`/`sections` are rejected
- The tap does **not** produce a button-reply webhook: the number arrives
  as a contacts message and is linked (or merged) onto the contact
  automatically
- Primarily for contacts who adopted a WhatsApp **username** — WhatsApp
  withholds their phone number from every webhook until they share it, so
  until then they are reachable on WhatsApp only, not SMS/RCS/email

## Example Request (Buttons)
```json
{
    "channel_id": "uuid",
    "contact_id": "uuid",
    "type": "buttons",
    "body": "Would you like to proceed with your order?",
    "buttons": [
        {"id": "confirm", "title": "Yes, confirm"},
        {"id": "cancel", "title": "No, cancel"},
        {"id": "help", "title": "Need help"}
    ]
}
```

## Example Request (List)
```json
{
    "channel_id": "uuid",
    "contact_id": "uuid",
    "type": "list",
    "body": "Please select a product category:",
    "button_text": "View Categories",
    "sections": [
        {
            "title": "Electronics",
            "rows": [
                {"id": "phones", "title": "Phones", "description": "Smartphones and accessories"},
                {"id": "laptops", "title": "Laptops", "description": "Notebooks and tablets"}
            ]
        }
    ]
}
```

**Required Scopes:** `messages:create`

reply_buttons.description: Send a message with up to 3 reply buttons. User taps a button to respond.

value.body: Would you like to schedule a callback?

list_menu.description: Send a scrollable list menu organized into sections. User selects one option.

value.body: Choose a topic for your support request:

request_contact_info.description: Show a single fixed-label button asking the user to share their own WhatsApp phone number. The label is set and localized by WhatsApp — pass no buttons.

value.body: To send you delivery updates by SMS, please share your phone number.

post.description:
Add a reaction (emoji) to a message.

Sends a reaction to the specified message on the messaging platform.
Supported on every channel whose capability matrix advertises reactions
(WhatsApp, Telegram, Messenger, Instagram, Live Chat); see the channel
capabilities endpoint for the per-channel `reactions` block.

## Important Notes
- The message's channel must support reactions (see channel capabilities)
- The message must have an external_id (platform message ID)
- Common emojis work best (thumbs up, heart, laugh, etc.)
- Telegram only accepts emojis from its fixed reaction set
- You can only have one reaction per message per sender

## Example Request
```json
{
    "emoji": "thumbs up"
}
```

**Required Scopes:** `messages:create`

delete.description:
Remove a reaction from a message.

Removes your reaction from the specified message on any channel that
supports reactions (WhatsApp, Telegram, Messenger, Instagram, Live Chat).
This is done by sending an empty emoji reaction.

**Required Scopes:** `messages:create`

post.description:
Send a sticker via WhatsApp.

Stickers are static or animated images in .webp format that can be sent
to WhatsApp contacts. Currently supported on **WhatsApp only**.

## Sticker Requirements
- **Format**: .webp only
- **Static stickers**: 512x512 pixels, max 100KB
- **Animated stickers**: 512x512 pixels, max 500KB

## Sending Methods
You can send a sticker using one of two methods:
1. **sticker_id**: Media ID of a previously uploaded sticker (preferred)
2. **sticker_url**: Direct URL to a .webp sticker file

## Example Request (by ID)
```json
{
    "channel_id": "uuid",
    "contact_id": "uuid",
    "sticker_id": "1234567890123456"
}
```

## Example Request (by URL)
```json
{
    "channel_id": "uuid",
    "contact_id": "uuid",
    "sticker_url": "https://example.com/stickers/happy.webp"
}
```

**Required Scopes:** `messages:create`

Send a carousel (multi-card) message via WhatsApp or Messenger.

This endpoint supports both platforms with different approaches:

## WhatsApp Carousels (Template-based)

WhatsApp carousels require a pre-approved template in Meta Business Manager.
Each card can have:
- **Header**: Image or video
- **Body**: Dynamic text parameters
- **Buttons**: Up to 2 buttons per card (max 10 cards)

### Example Request (WhatsApp)
```json
{
    "channel_id": "uuid",
    "contact_id": "uuid",
    "template_name": "product_catalog",
    "language": "en",
    "cards": [
        {
            "header": {"type": "image", "media_id": "123456789"},
            "body_parameters": [
                {"type": "text", "text": "Product A"},
                {"type": "text", "text": "$99.99"}
            ],
            "buttons": [
                {"type": "url", "index": 0, "parameters": [{"type": "text", "text": "product-a"}]}
            ]
        }
    ]
}
```

## Messenger Carousels (Generic Template)

Messenger carousels use the Generic Template format and don't require pre-approval.
Each element can have:
- **Title**: Card title (required)
- **Subtitle**: Card description
- **Image**: Card image URL
- **Default Action**: Action when card is tapped
- **Buttons**: Up to 3 buttons per element (max 10 elements)

### Example Request (Messenger)
```json
{
    "channel_id": "uuid",
    "contact_id": "uuid",
    "elements": [
        {
            "title": "Product A",
            "subtitle": "Great product for $99.99",
            "image_url": "https://example.com/product-a.jpg",
            "default_action": {
                "type": "web_url",
                "url": "https://example.com/products/a"
            },
            "buttons": [
                {"type": "web_url", "url": "https://example.com/buy/a", "title": "Buy Now"},
                {"type": "postback", "title": "More Info", "payload": "INFO_A"}
            ]
        }
    ]
}
```

## Supported Platforms
- **WhatsApp**: Use `template_name` + `cards`
- **Messenger**: Use `elements`

**Required Scopes:** `messages:create`

get.description:
List all conversations for the tenant with pagination.

**Required Scopes:** `conversations:read`

Respects multi-agent mode setting:
- Multi-agent mode: Shows all conversations
- Single-agent mode: Shows only assigned + unassigned (agents only)

**Response format:**
```json
{
    "items": [...],
    "pagination": {
        "total": 150,
        "page": 1,
        "page_size": 20,
        "total_pages": 8,
        "has_next": true,
        "has_prev": false
    }
}
```

Query parameters:
- page: Page number (1-indexed, default: 1)
- page_size: Items per page (1-100, default: 20)
- status: Filter by conversation status (open, closed)
- assigned_to: Filter by assignment ("me", "unassigned", or specific user_id)
- needs_reply: Filter for conversations needing a reply (true/false)
- filter: Alias for common filters ("unanswered" = needs_reply=true)
- contact_id: Filter by specific contact ID
- search: Search by contact name, phone, email, or conversation subject
- channel_type: Filter by channel type (whatsapp, telegram, sms, email, messenger, instagram, live_chat)

Snooze (postpone) a conversation.

**Required Scopes:** `conversations:update`

Snooze is a DERIVED state: the conversation ``status`` stays ``open`` /
``assigned`` — it simply drops off the **Open** tab and appears on the
**Snoozed** tab until ``snoozed_until`` passes (query-time expiry, no
background job). Once the timestamp passes it behaves like a normal open
conversation again.

Body:
- ``snoozed_until``: timezone-aware ISO datetime; MUST be in the future.
- ``reopen_on_message``: when true the inbound-message worker clears the
  snooze (returns it to Open) when a customer message arrives.

Emits the ``conversation.updated`` webhook event and a
``conversation_updated`` WebSocket broadcast so the UI moves the
conversation to the Snoozed tab in real time.

Cross-agent rules (when allow_messaging_other_agents_conversations is
False): only ADMIN/OWNER may snooze a conversation assigned to another
agent.

delete.description:
Clear a conversation's snooze (return it to the Open tab).

**Required Scopes:** `conversations:update`

Sets ``snoozed_until`` and ``snooze_reopen_on_message`` back to NULL.
Status is untouched. Idempotent — unsnoozing an already-unsnoozed
conversation succeeds and still emits ``conversation.updated`` so stale
client state converges.

Cross-agent rules (when allow_messaging_other_agents_conversations is
False): only ADMIN/OWNER may unsnooze a conversation assigned to another
agent.

post.description:
Manually trigger AI summary generation for a conversation.

**Required Scopes:** `conversations:update` (+ plan feature `ai_features`)

Start an async transcript export (PDF or ZIP) for a conversation.

**Required Scopes:** `conversations:read`

Creates a background job and returns it immediately with status ``queued``
(HTTP 202). Poll ``GET /conversations/{conversation_id}/transcript/{job_id}``
until ``status`` is ``completed`` (a ``download_url`` is then returned) or
``failed``.

Deduplication: a double-click / concurrent request is collapsed via a Redis
``SET NX EX`` lock, and a reload / fresh-completed request reuses the
existing job (an in-flight QUEUED/PROCESSING job, or a COMPLETED one from the
last few minutes) instead of enqueuing a duplicate.

get.description:
Poll the status of an async transcript export job.

**Required Scopes:** `conversations:read`

When ``status`` is ``completed`` the response includes the ``download_url``
(and ``storage_path``) written by the worker; when ``failed`` see
``error_message``.

post.description:
Email the conversation transcript to the contact (or any address).

**Required Scopes:** `conversations:update`

Offered when an agent closes a conversation (especially dead live-chat
tickets where the visitor left before reading the replies), but callable
for ANY conversation. Sends SYNCHRONOUSLY in-request: one branded HTML
email (tenant logo/name header, localized greeting, optional agent note,
the chat transcript, and the tenant's imprint/compliance footer) from the
selected ``EmailMailbox``.

Errors: 404 unknown conversation/mailbox (tenant-scoped), 400 invalid
email address / mailbox not sendable, 422 request validation, 502 the
email provider rejected the send.

get.description:
Full AI ticket summary for a single conversation, broken into the
three sections the contact-page timeline renders on expand:
``user_intent``, ``summary``, ``resolution``.

Lazy-loaded by the FE when a ``ticket_summary`` timeline row is
expanded — the timeline list itself only carries a 140-char
``summary_preview`` to keep the list payload small. Reads the text
directly off the ``Conversation`` SHARD row (no KB-doc / RAG fetch).

Returns 404 if the conversation does not exist in the caller's tenant
(tenant-isolated — never leaks cross-tenant ids). A conversation that
exists but was never summarized (or was reopened, which NULLs these
fields) returns 200 with all three sections ``null``.

**Required Scopes:** `knowledge_base:read`

Summarize a contact's previous conversations + advertise the merge target.

Redesigned (June 2026) to power a single-line history summary plus the
reopen-&-merge affordance, instead of a list of heavy per-conversation
cards. Returns CHEAP aggregates over the SAME contact's prior conversations
(excluding the current one):

  * `total_previous` — COUNT of prior conversations
  * `distinct_channel_count` — COUNT(DISTINCT channel_id)
  * `latest_previous_at` — MAX(last_message_at)
  * `merge_target_conversation_id` — the ONLY conversation this one may be
    merged into: the contact's OVERALL most-recent prior conversation, and
    ONLY when that immediately-previous conversation is on the SAME channel
    (`channel_id`) as the current one. Null when the immediately-previous
    conversation overall is on a different channel (even if an older
    same-channel prior exists). Computed by the SAME server-side helper the
    `POST /{id}/merge` endpoint enforces with, so the FE can never advertise
    a target the backend would reject.
  * `mergeable` — `merge_target_conversation_id is not None`

`items[]` is RETAINED in the response for backwards-compatibility but is
now ALWAYS returned EMPTY: the expensive per-item enrichment (bulk message
counts, last-message previews, channel-type hydration) is no longer
computed. The only former consumer (`ConversationHistoryBoundary.tsx`) is
being redesigned to use the aggregates. To list actual messages on a
channel, use `GET /api/v1/contacts/{contact_id}/messages`. The `limit`
query param is retained for compatibility but ignored.

All aggregates and the merge-target lookup respect contact-history
visibility: non-admin agents only see conversations on channels reachable
through their accessible Custom Inboxes. Admins/owners see everything.

**Required Scopes:** `conversations:read`

**Response format:**
```json
{ "items": [], "total_previous": 4, "distinct_channel_count": 2,
  "latest_previous_at": "2026-06-01T10:00:00Z", "mergeable": true,
  "merge_target_conversation_id": "..." }
```

post.description:
Reopen a closed conversation

**Required Scopes:** `conversations:update`

Merge a source conversation into this one and reopen it.

The path conversation (`conversation_id`) SURVIVES and is reopened; the
`source_conversation_id` from the body is merged in (all its messages,
notes, tags, attachments, etc. move over) and then permanently deleted.
Both conversations must belong to the SAME contact.

Reply routing adopts the source conversation's active channel so future
replies go to where the contact last reached us.

Server-side merge gating: the path conversation MUST be the single valid
merge target for the source — i.e. the contact's OVERALL most-recent PRIOR
conversation, and ONLY when that immediately-previous conversation is on the
SAME channel (`channel_id`) as the source. If the immediately-previous
conversation overall is on a DIFFERENT channel (even when an older
same-channel prior exists), there is NO valid target. This is the exact
target advertised by `GET /{id}/previous` (`merge_target_conversation_id`),
computed by the SAME helper, so the two can never diverge.

Rejections:
  * `400` — source == target (cannot merge into itself)
  * `404` — either conversation missing/not in tenant, or a channel not
    visible to the caller (contact-history visibility)
  * `409` — conversations belong to different contacts, OR the path
    conversation is not the valid merge target / no mergeable prior
    conversation exists on this channel

**Required Scopes:** `conversations:update`

get.description:
List channels available for switching from this conversation.

Returns all active switchable channels (WhatsApp, Telegram, Messenger,
Instagram) excluding the conversation's current channel. Used by the
frontend to render a channel picker before generating deeplinks.

Custom Inboxes security hardening (May 2026): for non-admin callers the
list is intersected with the channels reachable through the caller's
accessible Custom Inboxes. Admins/owners and tenants with zero inboxes
are unaffected.

**Required Scopes:** `conversations:read`

List email senders the caller may use for replying to this conversation.

Returns the user's accessible support-capable email connections, plus an
ACL-override entry when the conversation's default reply sender (the
receiving connection's ``outbound_provider``) is NOT already in that set.
The client pre-selects ``default_option_id`` and POSTs the chosen value
as ``MessageCreate.sender_id`` on the outbound send. The server
re-validates the choice on the send path.

Returns ``{"options": [], "default_option_id": null,
"default_reply_sender_id": null}`` for non-email conversations so clients
can rely on a stable response shape.

**Required Scopes:** `conversations:read`

post.description:
Generate channel switch deeplinks for a conversation.

Accepts a list of ``channel_ids`` to generate links for specific channels,
or omit to generate for all active switchable channels.

**Required Scopes:** `conversations:update`

Initiate a new outbound conversation with a contact. This endpoint allows agents to start new conversations from the UI. Behavior varies by channel: - **WhatsApp**: Checks 24h window. If closed, requires template message. - **Email**: Sends email with optional signature appended. - **Telegram/Messenger/Instagram**: Sends message directly. **Required Scopes:** `conversations:create` **Request Body:** ```json { "contact_id": "uuid", "channel_id": "uuid", "message_type": "text" | "template" | "email", // For text messages "content": "Hello...", // For WhatsApp templates "template": { "name": "hello_world", "language": "en", "components": [...] }, // For email "email": { "subject": "Re: Your inquiry", "body_html": "

Hello...

", "include_signature": true, "cc": [], "bcc": [] } } ``` **Response:** ```json { "conversation_id": "uuid", "message_id": "uuid", "channel_type": "whatsapp", "status": "sent" | "queued" | "failed" | "template_required", "requires_template": false, "window_status": { "in_window": true, "remaining_seconds": 3600 } } ```

Check for existing conversations without creating one.

This is Phase 1 of the two-phase conversation creation flow.
Use this endpoint to check if there are existing open or closed
conversations before deciding to create new or reopen existing.

**No webhooks are fired by this endpoint.**

After checking, call `/conversations/open-or-create` with:
- `action="create_new"` to create a new conversation
- `action="reopen_existing"` to reopen the closed conversation

**Required Scopes:** `conversations:create`

**Request Body:**
```json
{
    "contact_id": "uuid",
    "channel_id": "uuid"
}
```

**Response:**
```json
{
    "has_existing_open": true,
    "existing_open_conversation_id": "uuid",
    "has_existing_closed": false,
    "existing_closed_info": null,
    "channel_type": "whatsapp",
    "window_status": {
        "in_window": true,
        "requires_template": false,
        "last_customer_message_at": null,
        "window_end_at": "2026-01-17T10:00:00Z"
    }
}
```

Open an existing conversation or create a new one.

This is a simplified endpoint that does NOT send a message.
Use this when you want to navigate to a conversation and let the user
compose messages using the normal chat UI.

**Two-Phase API (Recommended):**
1. First call `/conversations/check-existing` to check for existing conversations
2. Then call this endpoint with `action` to control behavior:
   - `action="create_new"`: Always create new conversation (fires webhook)
   - `action="reopen_existing"`: Reopen closed conversation (fires conversation.reopened webhook)
   - `action="auto"` (default): Backwards compatible - may create without webhook if closed exists

For WhatsApp channels, the response includes window_status to indicate
whether templates are required (24h window closed).

**Required Scopes:** `conversations:create`

**Request Body:**
```json
{
    "contact_id": "uuid",
    "channel_id": "uuid",
    "action": "create_new"
}
```

**Response:**
```json
{
    "conversation_id": "uuid",
    "is_new": true,
    "is_reopened": false,
    "channel_type": "whatsapp",
    "window_status": {
        "in_window": true,
        "requires_template": false,
        "last_customer_message_at": "2026-01-16T10:00:00Z",
        "window_end_at": "2026-01-17T10:00:00Z"
    }
}
```

get.description:
Get current bot session status for a conversation.

**Required Scopes:** `conversations:read`

Returns:

`resubscribe_required` — i.e. the connection is otherwise fine, the Page is just
not subscribed to the `feed` webhook field that delivers post comments.

reconnecting), no permission is missing here: the stored Page token already
carries everything Facebook private replies need. So instead of sending the
customer to reconnect, we do it for them — this POSTs the Page's
`subscribed_apps` with the complete Messenger field list **plus `feed`** (a full
replace, never a merge; a Page that also backs a legacy page-backed Instagram
channel keeps `comments` on the union).

non-archived Messenger channel in the workspace. Tenant-scoped and idempotent.

verdict.

post.summary: Send a private reply to a comment
post.description:
Send a **private reply**: a direct message to the person who left a public
comment on your Instagram post or Facebook Page post.

Pass Meta's own comment id in the path — the value your `comment.received`
webhook delivers. The comment does not have to be stored in your workspace; if
it is not, supply `channel_id` in the body.

### What a private reply may contain

The two platforms differ, and this endpoint enforces the difference rather
than letting a field be silently dropped:

| Content | Instagram | Facebook Messenger |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | yes | yes |
| `buttons` | yes (up to 3, `url` or `postback`) | yes (up to 3, `url` or `postback`) |
| `quick_replies` | yes (up to 13) | yes (up to 13) |
| `image_url` | **no** — 400 | yes |

Buttons and quick replies are supported on **both** platforms — verified on
live accounts: they render for the recipient and taps arrive back as inbound
messages.

Images on Instagram are not accepted at all. On either platform, content the
private reply cannot carry belongs in a **follow-up** message: once the
recipient answers, the standard 24-hour messaging window opens and the normal
send API accepts buttons and media.

### Buttons

Each button is one of two kinds:

* **URL button** — `{"type": "url", "title": "Shop now", "url": "https://…"}`.
  Opens the link. Absolute **https** only. Nothing comes back to you.
* **Postback button** — `{"type": "postback", "title": "Get the code", …}`.
  Sends a value back to you when tapped, arriving as `meta.button_id` on the
  resulting inbound message. Either:
  * `"action": "start_flow", "flow_id": "…"` — the tap **starts that flow** for
    the person who tapped, or
  * `"payload": "your-own-value"` — an opaque value you match yourself.

A `start_flow` button may target any published flow **except** one whose
trigger is "Comment received": that trigger is reserved for the first message,
and this comment's single allowed private reply was already spent on the
message carrying the button.

### Rules Meta enforces

* **One private reply per comment, ever.** A second attempt returns `409`.
* **7-day window** from when the comment was created. After that, `410`.
* **Not available on ad comments** (Facebook). This is invisible until you
  send, so it surfaces as `422`.

### Billing

A private reply is a real Instagram/Messenger direct message and is billed
exactly like any other outbound message on that channel.

**🔐 Required Scopes:** `messages:create`

Facebook Page post — the ordinary "reply to this comment" action.

workspace, supply `channel_id` in the body.

Unlike a **private reply**, a public reply is comment-layer only: it does not
create a conversation, a contact or a `messages` row, and it is **not billed**
like a direct message. It also does not consume the one-per-comment private-reply
allowance — you can reply publicly and still send a private DM afterwards. There
is no time window and no duplicate suppression (Meta permits several public
replies to one comment).

Text only in v1 — no buttons, quick replies or media.

**Required Scopes:** `messages:create`

post.summary: Post a public reply and/or send a private DM in one call
post.description:
Post a public reply **and/or** send a private DM to a comment in one call.
Supply `public_text`, `private_text`, or both (at least one is required).

The private-DM fields (`buttons`, `quick_replies`, `image_url`) behave exactly
as on `POST /{comment_id}/private-reply` and apply only to the DM.

### Order and partial-failure contract

The public reply is posted **first**, then the private DM:

* **Public reply fails** → `502`, and the private DM is *not* attempted
  (nothing was sent).
* **Public reply succeeds, private DM fails** → `200` with
  `status: "partial"`: the public reply is already live and is returned in
  `public`, while `private` is `null` and `private_error` /
  `private_error_type` describe the DM failure. The public reply is never
  rolled back.
* **Private-only request (no `public_text`)** → the private-reply errors map to
  their usual HTTP statuses (`409` already-sent, `410` window, `422`
  not-eligible / invalid buttons, …), exactly like the standalone endpoint.
* **Everything sent** → `200` with `status: "sent"`.

Billing: the private DM is billed like any outbound message; the public reply is
not billed.

**Required Scopes:** `messages:create`

for the comment you answered publicly, answered on the phone, or simply decided
to skip. This is what stops the unanswered badge from being a number nobody can
ever drive to zero.

* `handled` — dealt with, no private reply sent.
* `ignored` — not actionable.
* `pending` — reopen; undoes either of the above.

the same transaction, not nudged up or down, so repeating this call — a
double-click, a retried request, flipping a comment back and forth — can never
make the badge drift.

reply message exists, and only sending one may assert that.

Instagram always requires media; `text` posts must not carry media. Every media

get.description:
Return insights for every PUBLISHED target of one authored post, served from a
per-target cache. Each target carries its own `last_refreshed_at`; the top-level
`last_refreshed_at` is the OLDEST of those (the staleness of the stalest number).

Numbers are NOT re-fetched on every load. A target that has never been cached
(`last_refreshed_at: null`) is populated LIVE once, on this first read, and
persisted so the next load is served from cache. Use
`POST /{post_id}/insights/refresh` to force a fresh read of all targets.

A target whose page lacks insights access degrades to `authorized: false` +
`error_code: insights_not_authorized`; a target whose channel was deleted
degrades to `insights_unavailable`; a target that never published (no
`meta_post_id`) is omitted.

**Required Scopes:** `campaigns:read`

post.description:
Force a LIVE re-fetch of Meta insights for every PUBLISHED target of one authored
post, UPSERT the per-target cache, and return the freshly-cached
`PostInsightsResponse`. Every readable target's `last_refreshed_at` is stamped to
now; the top-level `last_refreshed_at` is the oldest of the returned targets.

Degrade behavior matches `GET /{post_id}/insights` (unauthorized page →
`insights_not_authorized`, deleted channel → `insights_unavailable`, and the
degraded state is persisted too). A target that never published is omitted.

**Required Scopes:** `campaigns:read`

Validates the selection and every action against the tenant (tags/list/

signed `confirmation_token`. Submit the IDENTICAL `selection` + `actions`
together with that token to `/contacts/bulk-actions/execute` within
`expires_in_seconds` (~10 minutes).

Selection modes:
- `{"mode": "ids", "ids": [...]}` — explicit contact ids (max 10000).
- `{"mode": "filter", "filter": {...}}` — same params as `GET /contacts`
  (`search`, `include_live_chat`, `custom_field_id/value/value_to/op`,
  `list_id` + `list_subscription_status`/`list_subscription_channel`);
  `{}` targets ALL contacts.

Action types (executed in order per contact): `set_field`,
`set_custom_field`, `add_tags`, `remove_tags`, `add_to_list`.

Execute a previously previewed contact bulk action (202 Accepted).

**Required Scopes:** `contacts:update`

Requires the `confirmation_token` from `/contacts/bulk-actions/preview`
together with the IDENTICAL `selection` + `actions`. Errors:

- **400** `{"detail": {"code": "TOKEN_INVALID" | "TOKEN_EXPIRED", ...}}` —
  malformed/forged/expired token, or token minted for another tenant/user.
- **409** `{"detail": {"code": "PAYLOAD_MISMATCH", ...}}` — the submitted
  selection/actions differ from what was previewed.
- **409** `{"detail": {"code": "AFFECTED_COUNT_DRIFT", "affected_count": N,
  ...}}` — the match count changed since preview (any difference when the
  previewed count was < 100, otherwise more than ±2%). Re-preview and
  confirm again with the new count.

On success the run is recorded as a `BulkActionLog` audit row and executed
as a chunked background job; poll `poll_url` until `status` is
`completed`/`failed`. `affected_count` on the poll response is the running
total of actually-changed contacts.

post.description:
Create a new contact.

Honors the tenant's `duplicate_contact_mode` setting (or the optional
`duplicate_mode` body field for a per-request override):

- `auto_merge` (default): if a contact already exists with the same phone,
  email, or platform identifier, return that contact (oldest wins as
  primary). Incoming new methods/fields are merged into it.
- `allow_duplicates`: always create a new contact. The response includes a
  `potential_duplicates` list with any contacts sharing identifiers.
- `dont_allow_duplicates`: returns HTTP 409 with a `duplicates` array if
  a duplicate is detected; nothing is created.

`custom_fields` (optional): typed custom field values keyed by custom
field definition ID (preferred) or field `key`. Validated BEFORE anything
is written (422 per-field errors, see PATCH /contacts/{id}); written in the
same transaction as the contact. In `auto_merge`, when an existing contact
is matched, the given values OVERWRITE its values only if the caller also
holds `contacts:update`; otherwise they only fill fields that are empty
(fields that already have a value are skipped). null/empty entries are
ignored on create.

**Required Scopes:** `contacts:create`

get.description:
List contacts with pagination, search, server-side sorting, custom-field
and list-subscription filtering.

**Required Scopes:** `contacts:read`

Returns a paginated list of contacts matching the search criteria.
Each contact includes tags and custom fields.

**Sorting** (full-dataset, applied in SQL before pagination):
- `sort_by`: `created_at` (default), `name`, `email`, `custom_field`. Unknown
  values return 422.
- `sort_dir`: `asc` or `desc` (default `desc`).
- `sort_by=custom_field` requires `custom_field_id`. Contacts without a value
  for the field still appear (LEFT JOIN); NULLs sort first on asc, last on desc.

**Custom-field filter** (combinable with `search`):
The match strategy is selected SERVER-SIDE from the field's `field_type`
(looked up from `custom_field_definitions`), NOT from a client-trusted
operator. `custom_field_op` may narrow/override within what the type allows.

- `custom_field_id` alone → contacts that have ANY value for that field.
- **text** (and email/phone/url) → CONTAINS match (`value LIKE %v%`, with `%`
  and `_` in the input escaped to literals). This is the default for these
  types. (Behavior change: previously exact-match.)
- **select** → EXACT match; the supplied value must be one of the field's
  configured `options` (422 if not).
- **number** → operator-based via `custom_field_op`:
  `eq` (default), `gt`, `lt`, `gte`, `lte`, `between`. For `between`,
  `custom_field_value` is the lower bound and `custom_field_value_to` the
  (inclusive) upper bound; lower must be <= upper. Values must parse as
  numbers. Comparisons are numeric (TEXT values are regex-guarded then cast
  to DECIMAL, so non-numeric rows never match and never error).
- **other types** (boolean/date/datetime/location/multiselect/collection) →
  EXACT match (unchanged, backwards compatible).

`custom_field_op` allowlist: `eq`, `contains`, `gt`, `lt`, `gte`, `lte`,
`between`. Anything else is rejected by FastAPI (422). Numeric operators are
only valid for `number` fields and `contains` only for text-like fields;
incompatible combinations return 422.

The `custom_field_id` always validates the field belongs to the tenant
(422 if not).

**List-subscription filter** (combinable with `search` and the custom-field
filter — all filters are AND-ed, and `total` always reflects the filtered
set):

- `list_id` → a `lists.id`; validated to belong to the tenant (422 if not).
- `list_subscription_status` (default `subscribed` when `list_id` is set):
  - `subscribed` | `pending` | `unsubscribed` | `bounced` | `complained` →
    the contact has a subscription row with EXACTLY that status.
  - `any` → the contact has a subscription row for the list in ANY status.
  - `not_subscribed` → the contact has NO `subscribed` row for the list
    (i.e. not currently subscribed; includes contacts with no row at all).
- `list_subscription_channel` → optional narrowing on the subscription's
  channel (`email`, `sms`, `whatsapp`, `telegram`, `messenger`,
  `instagram`, `browser_push`). Subscription rows are PER CHANNEL, so this
  answers "subscribed to list X via WhatsApp". Applied inside the
  EXISTS/NOT EXISTS.
- Supplying `list_subscription_status` or `list_subscription_channel`
  WITHOUT `list_id` returns 422.

Contacts are matched with a correlated `EXISTS`/`NOT EXISTS`, so a contact
subscribed to the same list via several channels is returned ONCE.
For a DYNAMIC list (membership computed from segment conditions, no
subscription rows) the list's conditions are evaluated instead:
`subscribed`/`any` = matches the conditions, `not_subscribed` = does not;
the row-level statuses (`pending`/`unsubscribed`/`bounced`/`complained`)
cannot exist and match nothing.

**Tag-membership filter** (combinable with `search` and every other filter —
all AND-ed):

- `tag_id` → a `tags.id`; validated to belong to the tenant (422 if not).
  Restricts to contacts that carry that tag via the `contact_tags`
  association.
- `tag_id` is REPEATABLE (`?tag_id=a&tag_id=b`): several ids match contacts
  carrying ANY of them (OR / at-least-one). Duplicate ids are ignored.
- This filters by tag **id** (stable), never by tag name. It is a SEPARATE
  parameter from `search` on purpose: `search` matches name/email/phone/IDs
  only and never matches tags, so "find contacts by tag" uses `tag_id` and
  is not conflated with name search. When both are given, the text `search`
  is applied WITHIN the set of contacts carrying the tag(s).

**Response format:**
```json
{
    "items": [...],
    "pagination": {
        "total": 150,
        "page": 1,
        "page_size": 20,
        "total_pages": 8,
        "has_next": true,
        "has_prev": false
    }
}
```

is changed; `auto_merge` keeps this contact's current value and updates

`POST /contacts/{contact_id}/merge`.

post.description:
Add a new contact method to a contact.

Creates a new external identifier (phone, email, platform ID) linked to
this contact. For page-scoped types (messenger_id, instagram_id),
a channel_id is required.

If the proposed method's `(method_type, value, channel_id)` already
belongs to a *different* contact, this endpoint NEVER silently merges.
Instead it returns HTTP 409 with a machine-readable
`detail: "duplicate_contact_method"` body so the frontend can prompt the
user to either merge the two contacts or open the other contact.

This is true REGARDLESS of the tenant's `duplicate_contact_mode` default
(including `auto_merge`): an interactive method-add must never swallow an
unrelated contact. To actually merge, the client must make an explicit,
user-confirmed call to `POST /contacts/{contact_id}/merge` (which carries
its own `contacts:update` scope check and uses oldest-wins semantics).

The optional per-request `duplicate_mode` body field still tunes the
response shape on conflict, but none of the modes auto-merge here:

- `allow_duplicates`: returns the existing method on the OTHER contact
  unchanged (the unique constraint prevents duplicate ownership).
- `dont_allow_duplicates` / `auto_merge` (default) / omitted: returns the
  409 `duplicate_contact_method` conflict described above.

Adding a method that already exists on the SAME contact is idempotent.

**Required Scopes:** `contacts:update`

merged from multiple SHARD tables — see
:class:`app.services.contact_history_service.ContactHistoryService`
for the per-source query strategy and batch lookups.

Event types:

* ``conversation`` — one row per conversation (Activity mode).
* ``flow_run``     — one row per flow run (Activity mode).
* ``flow_message`` — flow-attributed messages only (legacy).
* ``message``      — every message for the contact regardless of
  flow attribution (Messages mode).
* ``scheduler``    — pending or fired scheduled sends (reminders,
  recurring sends, segment-blast materializations).
* ``ticket_summary`` — AI conversation summaries persisted as editable
  KB documents (``knowledge_base_documents`` filtered by the indexed
  ``contact_id`` column, ``document_type='ticket_summary'``). The
  ``document_id`` deep-links to the KB editor / raw GET-PUT endpoints.

**Required Scopes:** `contacts:read` AND `flows:read` AND `conversations:read` AND `scheduler:read` AND `knowledge_base:read`

get.description:
List pending contact merge suggestions for a conversation's contact.

**Required Scopes:** `conversations:read`

A suggestion is created when a live chat visitor enters an email address
or phone number (or the website passes a contact ID) that matches an
existing contact. The conversation is never linked to that contact
automatically: confirm the suggestion to merge the visitor into the
existing contact, or dismiss it to keep them separate.

`matched_value` is what the visitor entered and is not verified.

Suggestions are listed on both sides: in the visitor's conversations and in
every conversation of the matched contact. `perspective` says which side
this conversation's contact is on (`source` = the visitor, `target` = the
matched contact). Confirming or dismissing from either side resolves the
suggestion for both.

On the matched contact's side, `conversation_id` and `source_contact` are
null when you cannot open the visitor's conversation (for example because
of your inbox access). You can still confirm or dismiss the suggestion.

post.description:
Confirm a contact merge suggestion: merge the visitor contact into the matched contact.

**Required Scopes:** `contacts:update`

The request body must be `{"confirmed": true}`; anything else returns 422.
The unverified contact (`source_contact`) is merged into the existing
contact (`target_contact`), exactly like `POST /contacts/{contact_id}/merge`:
conversations, messages, notes, tags and contact methods move to the
surviving contact. This cannot be undone.

Returns 404 when the suggestion does not exist and 409 with
`error_code: suggestion_not_pending` when it was already confirmed or
dismissed. `conversation_id` and `source_contact` are null in the response
when you cannot open the visitor's conversation.

Dismiss a contact merge suggestion and keep both contacts separate.

**Required Scopes:** `contacts:update`

A dismissed pair is not suggested again. Returns 404 when the suggestion
does not exist and 409 with `error_code: suggestion_not_pending` when it
was already confirmed or dismissed. `conversation_id` and `source_contact`
are null in the response when you cannot open the visitor's conversation.

post.description:
Upload a file attachment

Args:
    file: The file to upload
    message_id: Optional message ID to associate with

Returns:
    Attachment ID and metadata

Security:
    - Validates file extension against blocklist
    - Validates file magic bytes match claimed MIME type
    - Enforces file size limits

**🔐 Required Scopes:** `messages:create`

Fetch a public URL server-side and store it as an attachment.

Returns the same shape as ``POST /upload`` so the response is
interchangeable. Caller can then pass the returned ``id`` /
``attachment_id`` in ``MessageCreate.attachments``.

Per-tenant URL dedup: if this tenant already has an attachment
whose ``source_url`` matches the requested ``url`` exactly, that
row is returned without re-fetching or re-uploading. To force a
re-fetch, vary the URL (e.g. add ``?t=12345``).

Security:
    - ``http://`` / ``https://`` only — ``file://``, ``gopher://``,
      ``data://`` etc. rejected.
    - Hostname resolved up-front; rejected if any A/AAAA record
      falls into loopback, RFC1918, link-local (incl. cloud
      metadata 169.254.169.254), ULA, reserved, or multicast.
    - Bytes validated against the same magic-byte sniffer as
      ``/upload`` AND against a stricter MIME allowlist
      (``URL_FETCH_ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES``).
    - 50 MB hard cap; streaming cut-off enforced even if the
      server lies in ``Content-Length``.

**Required Scopes:** ``messages:create``

Permanently removes the ``attachments`` row **and** its stored blob. This
is irreversible. Attachments are re-usable and carry no foreign key back
to the messages that referenced them, so deleting one that a previously
sent message still points at is allowed and expected — the message keeps
its metadata, the media simply stops resolving.

Args:
    attachment_id: ID of the attachment

Returns:
    ``204 No Content`` on success. ``404`` when the attachment does not
    exist or belongs to another tenant. ``500`` when the row exists but
    the delete itself failed (e.g. the storage backend errored) — in that
    case the row is left intact so the call can be retried.

**Required Scopes:** `messages:delete`

post.description:
Send a campaign immediately

**Required Scopes:** `campaigns:send`

Optional body `{"acknowledge_warmup_warning": true}` (no body = false).
A large WhatsApp campaign on a number that is still warming up is refused
with HTTP 409 `detail = {"code": "warmup_acknowledgement_required",
"message": ..., "warmup": <warm-up assessment>}` unless acknowledged or
split over days (`send_split_config`). Nothing is prepared or sent on 409.
A split plan that would run too long is refused with HTTP 422
`{"code": "split_plan_too_long", "message": ...}`.

With `send_split_config`, only day 1's batch is sent now; later batches
go out automatically (the response `split` block has `days_total`,
`next_batch_at`, `scheduled_count`).

**Response (200):** `{success, campaign_id, recipient_count,
published_count, dispatch, split, trial_recipient_cap, message}`. Messages
are sent in the background after the response. `published_count` is the
number of recipients queued to be sent now (all of them, or day 1 of a
split plan). `dispatch` is `"queued"` when that number is above 0, and
`"pending"` when nothing is due yet or queuing is retried automatically.

**Send speed and batches:** with `send_rate_limit` and/or
`send_batch_size` saved on the campaign, messages go out at the chosen
speed and, with a batch size, only the first batch is sent now. The
response then also has `pacing: {paced, batch_number, armed, remaining,
send_rate_limit, send_batch_size}` (`armed` = recipients in batch 1,
`remaining` = recipients waiting for later batches; `published_count` is
0 because the messages are released gradually). After each batch the
campaign is `paused` with `throttle_reason = "batch_complete"`; send the
next one with `POST /campaigns/{id}/send-next-batch`. Invalid saved
values are refused with HTTP 422 `{code, message}` (see
`PUT /campaigns/{id}`).

Only campaigns with status `draft`, `approved` or `scheduled` can be sent.

**Note:** Campaigns with status `in_review` or `rejected` cannot be sent
(HTTP 400). A campaign that is already sending, throttled, completed,
paused, failed or cancelled is refused with HTTP 409 -- re-posting here
would re-prepare the whole recipient list and send the campaign a second
time. Use `POST /campaigns/{id}/resume` for a paused or failed campaign.

schema.title: Response Send Campaign Api V1 Campaigns  Campaign Id  Send Post

post.description:
Pause a sending campaign

Also allowed while a split-sending campaign waits for its next daily batch
(`throttled` with `throttle_reason = "daily_batch_limit"`). A paused
campaign never resumes on its own -- use resume.

**Required Scopes:** `campaigns:send`

Resume a paused or failed campaign

For split-sending campaigns the remaining recipients are re-planned from
now: today's batch is sent, later batches continue on the following days.

Optional body `{"acknowledge_warmup_warning": true}` (no body = false).
A campaign the scheduler paused with `throttle_reason =
"warmup_acknowledgement_required"` (its warm-up acknowledgement was
missing or cleared by an edit), and any campaign resumed before its
recipients were prepared, passes the same WhatsApp warm-up gate as
`POST /send`: HTTP 409 `warmup_acknowledgement_required` unless
acknowledged; nothing changes on 409. Such a campaign is then dispatched
like a fresh send (recipients prepared, day 1 of a split plan published).
A campaign held because its audience grew since the acknowledgement
(`warmup_assessment.hold.kind = "audience_grew"`) always needs
`acknowledge_warmup_warning: true`. A successful resume clears
`warmup_assessment.hold`.

Resume continues the recipients that are still pending. It does not
re-send failed recipients; use `POST /campaigns/{id}/retry-failed` for
that. Sending continues in the background after the response.

Campaigns sent in batches: a campaign paused after finishing a batch
(`throttle_reason = "batch_complete"`) sends its next batch at the saved
batch size (the same as `POST /campaigns/{id}/send-next-batch` with an
empty body). Any other pause continues the current batch at the saved
send speed. A campaign sent in batches that ended as `completed` or
`failed` while recipients were still waiting is re-opened the same way.
While sending at a set speed or in batches is briefly unavailable, a
campaign that uses it returns HTTP 422 `send_pacing_unavailable`.

**Required Scopes:** `campaigns:send`

Send the next batch of a campaign sent in batches

Only for a campaign that finished a batch: `status = "paused"` with
`throttle_reason = "batch_complete"`, or one that ended as `completed` /
`failed` while recipients were still waiting (it continues its unfinished
batch first, if any). Anything else returns HTTP 409
`{"code": "campaign_not_awaiting_batch", "message": ...}` (also when two
requests race: only the first one sends a batch). HTTP 422
`send_pacing_unavailable` while batch sending is briefly unavailable.

Body (optional): `{"batch_size": 500}` sends 500 recipients now and saves
500 as the campaign's batch size (1-1,000,000; anything else is HTTP 422
`{"code": "send_batch_size_invalid", "message": ...}`); `{"all_remaining": true}` sends
everyone who is still waiting. An empty body sends the next batch at the
saved batch size. Recipients who opted out, unsubscribed or were blocked
since the campaign was prepared are skipped (`skipped_ineligible`).

**Response (200):** `{batch_number, armed, skipped_ineligible, remaining,
campaign}`. The batch is sent in the background at the campaign's send
speed; the campaign pauses again when the batch is done (or completes
when nobody is left).

**Required Scopes:** `campaigns:send`

get.description:
Per-batch delivery counts of a campaign sent in batches

One item per batch: `{batch_number, total, pending, sent, delivered,
read, failed, skipped}`, oldest batch first. `remaining` is the number of
recipients waiting for a later batch, `current_batch_number` the batch
the campaign is on and `send_batch_size` the saved batch size. A campaign
that is not sent in batches returns an empty list.

**Required Scopes:** `campaigns:read`

Send plan: speed, batches and estimated duration

Read-only estimate for the campaign's audience at its saved send speed
and batch size, or at the values given as query parameters (to preview a
change before saving it). `effective_rate_per_minute` is the requested
speed capped by what the campaign's channels can send, and
`rate_limited_by` says which of the two decides (`"campaign"` or
`"channel"`). `channels[]` lists each channel's recipients and maximum
messages per second. `eta_seconds` estimates the time to send everyone
who is left (time paused between batches not included);
`eta_seconds_per_batch` the time per batch. `pacing_available = false`
means send speed and batches are not available for this account yet.

Out-of-range query values return HTTP 422 `{code, message}`
(`send_rate_limit_out_of_range`, `send_batch_size_invalid`).

**Required Scopes:** `campaigns:read`

post.description:
Retry failed recipients of a campaign

Resets FAILED recipients back to pending and re-queues them for sending.
Designed for "top up, then retry": an SMS campaign that was paused because
the prepaid SMS balance was used up can be re-driven with
``{"error_codes": ["insufficient_sms_balance"]}`` once credit is available.
SMS recipients the carrier rejected or did not deliver are re-driven with
``{"error_codes": ["sms_rejected_by_carrier"]}`` / ``["sms_not_delivered"]``
(e.g. after the cause of an automatic pause was fixed).
SMS recipients that failed because the SMS provider temporarily limited
the sending rate are re-driven with ``{"error_codes": ["sms_rate_limited"]}``
-- lower the campaign's `send_rate_limit` or set a `send_batch_size`
first (`PUT /campaigns/{id}`) so the retry does not hit the limit again.
With no body (or an empty list) every failed recipient is retried.
Unknown codes return HTTP 422 listing the allowed codes.

Allowed on campaigns in status `completed`, `failed` or `paused`. A
`completed` or `failed` campaign returns to `sending` and any recipients
still pending are re-queued as well. A `paused` campaign STAYS paused: the
failed recipients are reset and go out together with the rest when the
campaign is resumed (`POST /campaigns/{id}/resume`). A retry never
resumes a paused campaign.

**Response:** `{"success": true, "id": "<campaign_id>", "requeued": <n>}`
where `requeued` is the number of failed recipients reset. When the
campaign was paused and stays paused the body also carries
`"paused": true` (the field is omitted otherwise).

**Errors:**
* HTTP 429 `{"code": "retry_failed_cooldown", "message", "retry_after_seconds"}`
  (plus a `Retry-After` header) when failed recipients of this campaign
  were retried less than 10 minutes ago.
* HTTP 422 `{"code": "retry_requires_send_speed", "message"}` when the
  campaign was paused because the SMS provider limited the sending rate
  and has no send speed / batch size yet: set `send_rate_limit` or
  `send_batch_size` with `PUT /campaigns/{id}` first.

For a split-sending campaign the reset recipients join the remaining
plan, re-planned from now like `POST /resume`: only today's batch is sent
immediately, the rest follows on the next days.

For a campaign sent in batches the reset recipients join the current
batch and are sent at the campaign's send speed.

**Required Scopes:** `campaigns:send`

Schedule a campaign for future sending.

Accepts a local datetime and IANA timezone string. The backend converts to UTC
for storage. The original timezone is preserved for display purposes.

The scheduled time must be at least 5 minutes in the future.

`acknowledge_warmup_warning` (default false): same WhatsApp warm-up rule as
`POST /send` -- 409 `warmup_acknowledgement_required` when required and not
given. The acknowledgement is stored; the scheduled dispatch does not
re-ask -- unless the audience, content, channels, template or split config
is edited afterwards: that clears the acknowledgement and the dispatch then
holds the campaign `paused` with `throttle_reason =
"warmup_acknowledgement_required"` until `POST /resume` acknowledges.
A split plan that would run too long: 422 `split_plan_too_long`.

**Required Scopes:** `campaigns:update`

get.description:
List recipients who opted out attributed to THIS messenger campaign.

Campaign-attributed opt-outs from the ``contact_subscription_events`` SHARD
ledger, split by source and confidence:

* LINK opt-outs (``method='link'``, ``attribution='exact'``) — recipient used
  this campaign's own unsubscribe surface; attribution is certain.
* KEYWORD opt-outs (``method='keyword'``, ``attribution='heuristic'``) — a
  "stop"-style keyword opt-out attributed to the last campaign on that channel
  within ``window_hours``. Only keyword opt-outs the heuristic matched to THIS
  campaign appear here.

``method_counts`` and ``attribution_counts`` cover the full result set;
``items`` is the requested page ordered by opt-out time DESC
(``page``/``page_size``, default 25). The UI labels link=exact vs
keyword=approximate off each item's ``attribution``.

Retry a single failed recipient of a messenger/newsletter campaign.

Calls the retry execution in ``CampaignService.retry_single_recipient`` and

delete.description:
Remove a single recipient from a messenger/newsletter campaign.

Hard-deletes the per-recipient row (tenant + campaign ownership validated),
then recomputes the campaign's denormalized counters and drops
`total_recipients` by 1. A recipient who was already sent the message
(sent / delivered / read) cannot be removed: HTTP 409.

**Required Scopes:** `campaigns:update`

post.description:
Bulk-remove all failed recipients from a messenger/newsletter campaign.

Hard-deletes every failed-group row for this campaign, recomputes the
campaign counters and drops `total_recipients` by the number removed. This
is DISTINCT from `POST /{campaign_id}/retry-failed`, which re-queues failed
recipients instead of deleting them.

**Required Scopes:** `campaigns:update`

Opt a messenger/newsletter recipient's contact out of this campaign's lists.

This is DISTINCT from `DELETE /{campaign_id}/recipients/{recipient_id}`
("Remove"), which only deletes the per-recipient row and does NOT change
subscription state. This endpoint resolves the recipient's contact, computes
the campaign's originating list(s) (`campaign_lists` ∩ the contact's
currently-subscribed lists) and opts the contact out of all of them via the
subscription chokepoint, writing the opt-out ledger with campaign attribution
(`method='manual'`).

- Recipient (or its campaign) not found for this tenant -> 404
- Recipient is an anonymous subscriber with no linked contact -> 422
- Contact subscribed to none of the campaign's lists (or the campaign targets
  no lists) -> 200 with an empty `unsubscribed_lists`
- Contact already opted out of all of the campaign's lists -> 200 with
  `already_unsubscribed: true`

**Required Scopes:** `campaigns:update`

post.description:
Create an independent copy of an existing flow as a fresh ``draft``.

The copy mirrors every behaviour-defining field on the source — full
``definition`` JSON (trigger, schedule, nodes, edges, node configs,
re-entry policy), ``description``, and the channel/tag/etc. config
nested inside ``definition``. Node ids are regenerated and every
internal reference (edges, ``entry_node_id``, config-level
``*_node_id`` keys) is remapped so the copy is fully self-consistent.

Resets on the copy:

* ``status`` is ``draft`` regardless of source status — so nothing
  fires until the user explicitly publishes the copy.
* Fresh ``id`` / ``created_at`` / ``updated_at``.
* No run history (``flow_runs`` rows are not copied).

Body is optional. When ``name`` is omitted the default is
``"<source.name> (copy)"``. Source flows in any status (draft,
published, paused, archived) can be duplicated.

Returns 404 when the source flow doesn't exist on the caller's tenant.

**Required Scopes:** `flows:write`

patch.description:
Re-order flow trigger priorities for the current tenant.

Accepts EITHER an ordered ``flow_ids`` list (server assigns
``priority = position``, 0-based, so the first id wins) OR an explicit
``items: [{flow_id, priority}]`` list. Exactly one shape must be supplied.
Lower ``priority`` = higher precedence (evaluated first when multiple flows
match the same inbound event).

All ids are validated to belong to this tenant BEFORE any write; the whole
batch is persisted in a single transaction (fail-closed — if any id is not
owned by the tenant, nothing is written and a 404 is returned).

**Required Scopes:** `flows:write`

**Database:** SHARD (``flows`` — tenant-filtered on every row).

Returns the resulting ordering: ``{"items": [{flow_id, name, priority},
...]}`` sorted by ``priority`` ASC.

post.description:
Publish a flow.

Runs the **stricter** publish-time validation pass:

- Every node reachable from ``entry_node_id``.
- No orphan nodes.
- Every condition has both ``yes_node_id`` + ``no_node_id`` wired.
- No infinite cycles in synchronous-only paths (Delay/Send-bearing
  cycles are allowed — they're the legitimate "drip every day" pattern).

Returns ``400 FLOW_DEFINITION_INVALID`` with the full error list on
failure. Returns ``409`` when trying to publish an archived flow.

**Required Scopes:** `flows:publish`

Pause a published flow.

New ``POST /flows/{id}/runs`` calls return ``409`` while paused
(``FlowEngineService.start_run`` requires PUBLISHED). In-flight runs
continue — operators want to drain.

**Required Scopes:** `flows:write`

delete.description:
Permanently delete a flow — irreversible, destroys run history.

Distinct from ``DELETE /flows/{id}``, which soft-archives (reversible
via ``POST /flows/{id}/unarchive``). This endpoint removes the
``flows`` row AND every child row: ``flow_runs``, ``flow_run_steps``,
``flow_run_waits``. No FK cascades exist on the flow tables, so the
service deletes children explicitly inside one transaction. Keyword-bot
wiring that pointed at the flow is detached (set to NULL) rather than
deleted. Conversation ``messages`` and ``tracked_links`` produced by
the flow are KEPT — they are real history and their flow attribution
readers are already best-effort.

Refuses with ``409`` rather than corrupting state:

* flow is ``published`` — pause or archive it first;
* the flow has in-flight runs (``running``/``waiting``) — stop them or
  let them finish. Flow-Test-Mode runs never block.

The ``detail`` string names which of the two it is and, for in-flight
runs, how many. ``GET /flows/{id}`` (and the flows list) expose
``run_count`` so the UI can warn how many runs a delete would destroy
BEFORE calling this.

Returns ``404`` when the flow does not exist for this tenant — this is
NOT idempotent-on-missing like archive, because "already gone" and
"never yours" must not be distinguishable across tenants.

**Required Scopes:** `flows:write`

Batch opt-in / opt-out / net-change counts for every list in the window.

Returns a row for EVERY list the tenant has (zeros for lists with no
subscription activity) so the frontend can map results by ``list_id``.

- ``opt_ins`` — subscriptions whose confirmed-opt-in timestamp
  (``opt_in_confirmed_at``) falls in the window.
- ``opt_outs`` — subscriptions with status ``unsubscribed`` whose
  ``unsubscribed_at`` falls in the window.

Counts are a current-state approximation (a re-subscribe NULLs
``unsubscribed_at``), so churny opt-outs are undercounted.

post.description:
Upload a file (PDF, DOCX, etc.) as a knowledge base document.

**Required Scopes:** `knowledge_base:create`

Supported file types: PDF, DOCX, TXT, MD.

**Async pipeline (B-4):**
1. The file bytes are uploaded to GCS synchronously.
2. A row is inserted with ``status='pending_ingestion'`` and a fresh ``job_id``.
3. A ``kb_add_file`` Pub/Sub message is published to the KB administration
   worker which performs the Vertex AI RAG import.
4. This endpoint returns 202 immediately. Poll GET ``/jobs/{job_id}`` or
   GET ``/documents/{id}`` to observe when ``status`` transitions to
   ``ready`` (or ``failed`` with ``last_error`` populated).

Upload multiple files at once to the knowledge base.

**Required Scopes:** `knowledge_base:create`

Up to 200 files per request. Each file is uploaded to GCS, gets its own
``status='pending_ingestion'`` DB row + ``job_id``, and is dispatched to
the KB administration worker as an independent ``kb_add_file`` Pub/Sub
message. Partial success is possible — a per-file GCS or publish failure
rolls back only that file's row and surfaces as a ``success=false`` entry.

Supported file types: PDF, DOCX, TXT, MD.

Pre-crawl sanity check for a website URL (always HTTP 200).

**Required Scopes:** `knowledge_base:admin`

Validates the URL (scheme, hostname with a real domain ending, DNS, private
network block, reachability) and, when reachable, detects a sitemap and
counts the pages it lists so the UI can show "sitemap found, N pages"
before the user starts the crawl.

`valid=false` ⇒ `error_code` is one of `invalid_url`, `invalid_hostname`,
`dns_unresolvable`, `blocked`, `unreachable`, `timeout`, `http_error`.
The same checks run server-side on every crawl start; this endpoint only
lets the UI show the outcome early.

Start asynchronous website crawl job.

**Required Scopes:** `knowledge_base:admin`

This endpoint immediately returns a job_id that can be used to track progress.
The actual crawling happens in a Pub/Sub background worker.

Use GET /documents/crawl/{job_id}/status to check progress.

Get status of website crawl job.

Poll this endpoint to track progress of an async crawl operation.

post.description:
Cancel a running website crawl job.

delete.description:
Queue an async delete for a knowledge base document.

**Required Scopes:** `knowledge_base:delete`

**Async pipeline (B-4):**
1. The row is flipped to ``status='deleting'`` with a fresh ``job_id``.
2. A ``kb_delete_file`` Pub/Sub message is published.
3. The KB administration worker performs the RAG file delete and then
   removes the row. Poll GET ``/jobs/{job_id}`` to observe completion.

post.description:
Retry ingestion for a single knowledge base document.

**Required Scopes:** `knowledge_base:create`

Retryable documents are either ``status='failed'`` OR a *stuck*
``status='pending_ingestion'`` row — one left un-imported under a crawl/
ingestion job that has since finished (see ``_pending_ingestion_is_stuck``:
old enough and owned by no still-running job). Any other status — including
a ``pending_ingestion`` row whose ingestion job is still running — returns
409. The GCS object already exists from the original upload, so this does
NOT re-upload the file bytes — it re-derives the ``gcs_uri`` + folder corpus
from the stored metadata, flips the row to ``status='pending_ingestion'``
with a fresh ``job_id`` and ``last_error=NULL``, and re-publishes the
``kb_add_file`` Pub/Sub message. Returns the updated document (202).

Retry every failed document in a folder.

**Required Scopes:** `knowledge_base:create`

Re-queues every retryable document in the folder using the same per-document
logic as the single retry endpoint: all ``status='failed'`` documents, plus
any ``status='pending_ingestion'`` document that is *stuck* — left un-imported
under a crawl/ingestion job that has since finished (see
``_pending_ingestion_is_stuck``). A ``pending_ingestion`` row still owned by a
running job is skipped, never re-queued. A folder with nothing to retry is not
an error — it returns ``retried_count: 0``.

Returns ``{"success": true, "retried_count": N}``.

Queue async deletion for many documents at once.

**Required Scopes:** `knowledge_base:delete`

Transactional safety: rows are flipped to ``status='deleting'`` in a
single transaction, then one ``kb_delete_file`` Pub/Sub message is
published per document. If publishing fails mid-batch, we revert all
affected rows back to ``status='ready'`` and return 500.

delete.description:
Queue async deletion for a folder and all of its documents.

**Required Scopes:** `knowledge_base:delete`

1. The folder is flipped to ``status='deleting'``.
2. All contained documents are flipped to ``status='deleting'`` and each
   is dispatched as a ``kb_delete_file`` job.
3. A single ``kb_delete_folder_finalize`` job is published; the worker
   polls for document drain, then deletes the Vertex AI corpus and the
   folder row.

System folders cannot be deleted.

post.description:
Re-crawl a domain with non-destructive crawl-then-reconcile.

**Modes:**
- `existing_pages`: Re-crawl the exact URLs from previous crawl history (faster, predictable scope)
- `full_rescan`: Re-discover pages via sitemap/BFS from scratch (finds new pages, more thorough)

Both modes update existing documents in-place by matching source_url, create new documents
for newly discovered pages, and remove orphaned documents only after successful completion.
Existing content remains intact if the crawl fails mid-way.

**Note:** Domains must be at least 14 days old to be eligible for re-crawl.

Stream the raw UTF-8 text content of an editable KB document from GCS.

**Required Scopes:** `knowledge_base:read`

Supported document types: ``manual``, ``uploaded_doc``, ``faq`` — and only
for extensions ``.md`` / ``.txt`` / ``.html``. Returns 400 for PDFs,
images, crawled website pages, or any other non-editable type.

For inline-created FAQ/manual docs (no filename on record) the raw
content is served from ``upload_metadata.content`` to avoid a spurious
GCS miss for rows that predate the GCS-only flow.

put.description:
Replace the raw text content of an editable KB document.

**Required Scopes:** `knowledge_base:update`

Behaviour:
  1. Validates size (≤ 1 MB) — returns 413 otherwise.
  2. Validates that the document type + extension are editable
     (otherwise 400, same rules as GET ``/raw``).
  3. Uploads the new bytes to GCS (same path pattern as
     ``upload_to_gcs()`` — ``rag_uploads/{tenant_id}/doc_{id}_{uuid}.{ext}``).
  4. Updates the DB row: ``gemini_file_name`` / ``upload_metadata.gcs_uri``
     point at the new blob, ``status`` → ``pending_ingestion``, a fresh
     ``job_id`` is set, ``updated_at`` = ``utc_now()``.
  5. Publishes a ``kb_add_file`` message to ``PUBSUB_TOPIC_KB_ADMINISTRATION``
     so the KB administration worker performs the Vertex AI RAG import.
     When ingestion completes, status transitions back to ``ready``.

HTML is stored as-is — no sanitization (user controls the content).

Consolidate duplicate FAQ entries into one.

Approval-gated and NEVER automatic — nothing in generation/migration/

(merged_stats, files that would be deleted, question variants). An execute
(``dry_run=false``) is additionally gated by the server-side
``FAQ_MERGE_EXECUTION_ENABLED`` flag; while that flag is off the execute path
returns **403** so the destructive RAG/GCS delete cannot run by accident
against the shared production database. See ``faq_merge_service`` for the full
safety model (three independent guards + the orphan basename guardrail).

On execute the winner inherits summed usage stats, unioned rating mass
(quality recomputed via the Wilson lower bound), unioned source
conversations, and the losers' question phrasings; losers are de-indexed and
archived with a merge tombstone; the winner is re-synced to RAG.

`status` and there is no separate publish endpoint. Because the corpus
follows `status`, flipping a draft to `published` is what indexes it and
puts it in front of customers.

Every field the schema accepts is forwarded to the service. It previously
forwarded only `question`/`answer`, so a publish returned 200 while the
entry stayed a draft, unindexed and invisible to the assistant.

The Vertex round-trip (upload + import, tens of seconds) is NOT held open
inside the request: a standalone entry's re-index is handed to the
`resync_faq_entry` job on the KB administration worker — the same path the
create route and the review queue use. The response returns as soon as the
row is committed, so an entry can read `published` for a few seconds before
`rag_file_name` is populated. The job re-reads the entry's current status,
so rapid publish/unpublish pairs converge on the last write instead of
racing.

A legacy document-scoped entry additionally schedules a recompile of its
parent document.

Read-only and side-effect free — it loads the tenant's ticket summaries and

writes nothing. This is what the "migrate history" button shows before the

post.description:
Start (or preview) the bulk migration of ticket summaries into FAQ drafts.

`dry_run=true` is handled **inline and never enqueues anything**: it loads
and clusters the summaries and returns what it would have processed. No
Gemini call, no row written, no folder touched — so it cannot possibly
change the tenant's knowledge base. Everything else publishes one
`migrate_ticket_summaries` job; the worker processes a bounded number of
clusters and re-enqueues itself until nothing is left, so this returns
immediately and the UI polls `/faq-migration/status`.

Everything the migration imports lands as a **draft**, whatever the
tenant's `faq_generation_mode` says.

**409** when a migration is already in flight — the job chain would
otherwise fork, double-billing the tenant for the same clusters. The
response body carries the run that is holding it:

    {"detail": {"code": "migration_already_running",
                "message": "...",
                "run": {...} | null,
                "last_activity_at": "...Z" | null}}

Pass `force=true` to override, once you know the other run is dead.

**Required Scopes:** `knowledge_base:manage`

get.description:
Progress of the bulk migration, from what it has actually persisted.

Poll-safe: counts are read back from the rows the migration wrote, with no
clustering and no LLM call.

**What is and is not knowable.** The migration keeps no run record and no
cursor — it is resumable purely from `faq_items.source_conversation_ids`.
So the backend can substantiate exactly one ratio,
`percent_summaries_processed` (summaries consumed / summaries that exist),
and it deliberately reports nothing about clusters remaining or time
left, because nothing persists that. `running` is likewise an inference
(`running_evidence` says from what), not a recorded state.

**Required Scopes:** `knowledge_base:read`

post.description:
Rate an AI answer 👍 / 👎 / ✗ (upsert — re-rating replaces).

``down`` and ``wrong`` REQUIRE ``reason_category``: a verdict with no
reason cannot drive the correction loop and only produces noise in the
score.

A KB correction is opened (and an analysis job enqueued) when:

* the verdict is ``wrong`` — always; or
* the verdict is ``down`` **and** it carries substantive text in
  ``comment`` and/or ``better_answer``.

A bare 👎 with no prose stays a cheap score signal and spawns no job.
``correction_opened`` / ``correction_id`` in the response tell the caller
which happened, so the UI can confirm it and link to the review queue.

Opening a correction never publishes anything by itself: a ``down``-born
correction is review-only even for tenants in ``kb_correction_mode=auto``.

Returns the recomputed scores of every FAQ entry the verdict touched, so
the UI can reflect the consequence immediately.

Send or schedule email campaign.

- Send speed and batches: with a `send_rate_limit` and/or
  `send_batch_size` saved on the campaign, the emails go out at that
  speed and in batches of that size. After each batch the campaign pauses
  (`status = "paused"`, `throttle_reason = "batch_complete"`) until
  `POST /email-campaigns/{id}/send-next-batch`. A saved batch size that
  cannot be used returns HTTP 422 `{code, message}` before anything is
  sent (`send_pacing_unavailable`, `send_batch_size_invalid`).
- HTTP 409 "This campaign is already being sent" when the campaign is
  already `sending` / `throttled` / `paused`, or a concurrent request (a
  second click, the scheduled send) started it first -- nothing is queued
  twice. HTTP 409 "This campaign was paused or cancelled while it was
  being prepared for sending. Refresh and try again." when that happened
  during the send.

for storage. The original timezone is preserved for display purposes.

The scheduled time must be at least 5 minutes in the future.

allowing the user to edit and reschedule. The timezone is preserved

Cancel scheduled, sending or paused campaign.

- Updates status to CANCELLED (also from `paused`, including a campaign
  waiting for its next batch)
- Stops further Pub/Sub processing
- Recipients still waiting for a later batch are not sent
- Does NOT refund balance (already deducted)

Needs the same scope as send / pause / resume (`campaigns:send`):
stopping a send is a send-control action, not a content edit.

**Required Scopes:** `campaigns:send`

Pause a sending email campaign

Only a campaign in `sending` or `throttled` can be paused (anything else
returns HTTP 400). Emails already handed to the email provider are not
recalled; everyone else waits until `POST /email-campaigns/{id}/resume`.

**Required Scopes:** `campaigns:send`

Resume a paused email campaign

Only a `paused` campaign can be resumed (anything else returns HTTP 400).
Sending continues with everyone who has not been sent yet. If a send
speed or batch size was saved while the campaign was paused, it applies
from now on. A campaign that finished a batch
(`throttle_reason = "batch_complete"`) sends its next batch, exactly
like `POST /email-campaigns/{id}/send-next-batch` with an empty body.
A campaign sent in batches that ended as `completed` or `failed` while
recipients were still waiting is re-opened the same way. HTTP 422
`send_pacing_unavailable` while sending at a set speed or in batches is
briefly unavailable.

**Required Scopes:** `campaigns:send`

Send the next batch of an email campaign sent in batches

Only for a campaign that finished a batch: `status = "paused"` with
`throttle_reason = "batch_complete"`, or one that ended as `completed` /
`failed` while recipients were still waiting (it continues its unfinished
batch first, if any). HTTP 422 `send_pacing_unavailable` while batch
sending is briefly unavailable. Anything else returns HTTP 409
`{"code": "campaign_not_awaiting_batch", "message": ...}` (also when two
requests race: only the first one sends a batch).

Body (optional): `{"batch_size": 500}` sends 500 recipients now and saves
500 as the campaign's batch size (1-1,000,000; anything else is HTTP 422
`{"code": "send_batch_size_invalid", "message": ...}`);
`{"all_remaining": true}` sends everyone who is still waiting. An empty
body sends the next batch at the saved batch size. Recipients who
unsubscribed, bounced or were suppressed
since the campaign was prepared are skipped (`skipped_ineligible`).

**Response (200):** `{batch_number, armed, skipped_ineligible, remaining,
campaign}`.

**Required Scopes:** `campaigns:send`
