post.description:
Import contacts from CSV file

**Required Scopes:** `contacts:create`

Imports contacts from a CSV file. At least one of `email`, `phone`,
`whatsapp_id`, `display_name`, `first_name`, or `last_name` is
required per row. Optionally creates email subscriptions for contacts
that have an email address.

**Supported columns (all optional except for the row anchor above):**

| Column | Maps to | Normalization |
|--------|---------|---------------|
| `first_name` | `Contact.first_name` | trim |
| `last_name` | `Contact.last_name` | trim |
| `display_name` (alias: `name`) | `Contact.name` | trim; falls back to `"{first} {last}"` |
| `email` | `Contact.email` + `ContactMethod` (EMAIL) | trim + lowercase |
| `phone` | `Contact.phone` + `ContactMethod` (PHONE) | parsed via libphonenumber to E.164 |
| `whatsapp_id` | `ContactMethod` (WHATSAPP_ID) | digits-only (strips `+`, spaces, formatting) |
| `languages` | `Contact.languages` | comma-separated ISO 639-1 codes; quote the cell if more than one |
| `birthday` | `Contact.birthday` | `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `tags` | `contact_tags` (many-to-many) | comma-separated; quote the cell; missing tags auto-created |
| `linkedin` | `ContactMethod` (LINKEDIN) | trim |
| `instagram_handle` | `ContactMethod` (INSTAGRAM_HANDLE) | trim; strips leading `@` |
| `facebook` | `ContactMethod` (FACEBOOK) | trim |
| `homepage` | `ContactMethod` (HOMEPAGE) | trim |
| `custom_fields` | `Contact.custom_data` | JSON object string |

Header names are matched case-insensitively. Common aliases are
accepted out-of-the-box: `firstname`/`given` → `first_name`,
`lastname`/`surname` → `last_name`, `full name` → `display_name`,
`lang`/`language` → `languages`, `dob`/`born` → `birthday`,
`wa`/`wa_id` → `whatsapp_id`, `ig` → `instagram_handle`,
`fb` → `facebook`, `website`/`url` → `homepage`, `labels` → `tags`.

**CSV quoting:** Cells containing commas (e.g. multiple tags or
languages) **must be quoted** per RFC 4180.

**Example CSV:**
```
first_name,last_name,display_name,email,phone,whatsapp_id,languages,birthday,tags,linkedin,instagram_handle,facebook,homepage,custom_fields
John,Doe,John Doe,john.doe@acme.com,+1 234 567 89,+1 234 567 89,"en,de",1990-04-12,"vip,lead",john-doe,@johndoe,john.doe.42,https://acme.com,"{"company":"Acme Corp"}"
Jane,Smith,,jane@acme.com,+49 30 12345678,4930123456789,de,,"customer",,,,,
,,Acme Bot,,,,en,,"bot",,,,,
```

**Subscription creation:**
- Set `create_subscription=true` to create email subscriptions
- Requires `optin_confirmed=true` when creating subscriptions (GDPR/CAN-SPAM compliance)
- Subscriptions only created for contacts with a valid email address
- Use `list_ids` to subscribe to multiple lists (comma-separated)

**Process:**
1. Validates the CSV has at least one anchor column (see above).
2. Validates and normalizes each row (phone → E.164, whatsapp_id
   → digits-only, email → lowercase, birthday → date).
3. Checks for duplicates by email and phone within tenant (subject
   to the tenant's `duplicate_contact_mode`).
4. Creates contacts and one `ContactMethod` row per non-empty
   method field. Tags are looked up or auto-created within the
   tenant and attached to the contact.
5. Optionally creates email subscriptions and adds to specified lists.

**Returns:**
- Summary with total, imported, duplicates, invalid_rows, and errors

Returns connection status and any errors.

Trigger a manual sync for an email integration.

**Required Scopes:** `email_integrations:update`

This is typically used for SMTP/IMAP or Gmail integrations to fetch new emails.

get.description:
Get DNS records required for domain verification.

**Required Scopes:** `email_integrations:read`

Returns DKIM, SPF, and DMARC records that need to be set in DNS.

schema.title: Response Get Dns Records Api V1 Email Integrations  Integration Id  Dns Records Get

post.description:
Trigger DNS verification check.

**Required Scopes:** `email_integrations:update`

Checks if the required DNS records have been properly configured.

Start domain verification for an SES managed integration.

**Required Scopes:** `email_integrations:update`

This:
1. Creates an email identity for the domain in SES
2. Returns DNS records (DKIM, SPF, DMARC) that need to be added
3. Associates the domain with the SES tenant once verified

The customer must add these DNS records to their domain before emails can be sent.

get.description:
Check domain verification status for an SES managed integration.

**Required Scopes:** `email_integrations:read`

Returns the current verification status and DNS records.

post.description:
Pause email sending for an SES managed integration.

**Required Scopes:** `email_integrations:update`

This manually pauses the SES tenant, stopping all email sending.
Use this if you need to temporarily disable sending (e.g., suspected abuse).

Resume email sending for an SES managed integration.

**Required Scopes:** `email_integrations:update`

This resumes sending for a paused SES tenant.

Note: If the tenant was auto-paused due to reputation issues,
you should address the underlying problem before resuming.

Add a Gmail send-as alias.

Adds the alias email and creates a corresponding mailbox.
The alias MUST be configured in Gmail under Settings > Accounts and Import > Send mail as,
otherwise Gmail will silently send from the primary email instead.

**Required Scopes:** `email_integrations:update`

delete.description:
Remove a verified Gmail send-as alias.

Deactivates the corresponding mailbox (preserves history).

**Required Scopes:** `email_integrations:update`

post.description:
Trigger a manual sync for a Gmail integration.

**Required Scopes:** `email_integrations:update`

This will:
1. Fetch new messages from Gmail since last sync
2. Process and store them in the system
3. Update the integration's history ID

get.description:
Get the full email thread for a conversation.

**Required Scopes:** `email_integrations:read` OR `conversations:read`

Returns all email messages associated with this conversation, including:
- RFC 5322 headers (Message-ID, In-Reply-To, References)
- From, To, CC, BCC addresses
- Subject and body (text + signed URL for HTML)
- Attachments with download URLs
- Thread relationships for proper email client display

This is the primary endpoint for the email thread view in Conversations UI.

post.summary: Compose and send new outbound email
post.description:
Compose and send a new outbound email (not a reply).

**Required Scopes:** `email_integrations:update` OR `messages:create`

Use this endpoint for initiating new email conversations where there's
no existing message to reply to.

Features:
- Plain text and/or HTML body support (rich text)
- Subject line required
- CC/BCC support
- Attachment support via attachment IDs

The email is sent via the conversation's associated email integration.

post.summary: Compose and send email from an EmailContent template
post.description:
Compose and send an outbound email using a pre-designed EmailContent template.

**Required Scopes:** `email_integrations:update` OR `messages:create`

The template is compiled with the conversation contact's data (name, email, phone)
substituted into template variables. Optional variable_overrides allow the caller
to override or supplement template variable values before compilation.

Uses the same 3-tier sending identity resolution as compose-email:
mailbox -> integration -> channel.

post.summary: Preview an EmailContent template with conversation contact data
post.description:
Preview an EmailContent template compiled with the conversation contact's data.

**Required Scopes:** `email_integrations:read`

Returns the fully compiled HTML and subject line with all template variables
replaced using the actual contact data from the conversation. Also resolves
the sending identity so the frontend can display the from address.

Use this endpoint to show a live preview before sending via compose-from-template.

get.summary: Get email summary for conversation sidebar
get.description:
Get email summary for the conversation sidebar.

**Required Scopes:** `email_integrations:read` OR `conversations:read`

Returns:
- Whether this conversation has email messages
- Total message and attachment counts
- Latest email information
- All unique participants in the thread
- Email integration type and ID

This is a lightweight endpoint for displaying email info in the sidebar.

Get detailed information for a single email message.

**Required Scopes:** `email_integrations:read`

Returns full email details including:
- All headers
- Full text body
- Signed URL for HTML body
- Attachment list with download URLs

Use this endpoint when expanding a collapsed email in the thread view.

delete.description:
Permanently delete an email message.

This action cannot be undone. Consider using hide instead for soft-delete.

**Required Scopes:** `email_integrations:delete`

get.summary: Get all messages in email thread
get.description:
Get all messages in the same thread as the specified email message.

**Required Scopes:** `email_integrations:read`

This loads the full email chain using the thread_id from the specified message.
Useful for viewing the complete thread context.

post.description:
Send a reply to an email message.

**Required Scopes:** `email_integrations:update` OR `messages:create`

Features:
- Plain text and/or HTML body support (rich text)
- CC/BCC handling with option to preserve original CCs
- Reply-all option
- Attachment support via attachment IDs
- Automatic subject line (Re: original) with override option

The reply is queued for sending via the configured email integration.
Thread headers (In-Reply-To, References) are automatically set.

post.summary: Upload inline image for rich text email
post.description: Upload an inline image for use in rich text email replies. **Required Scopes:** `email_integrations:update` Returns: - attachment_id: ID to reference in reply - content_id: CID for use in HTML (e.g., ``) - url: Signed URL for preview in composer Usage in HTML body: ```html ``` Then include the attachment_id in the reply request's attachment_ids array.

post.summary: Upload inline image via multipart form
post.description:
Upload an inline image via multipart form data.

**Required Scopes:** `email_integrations:update`

This is an alternative to the raw body upload endpoint,
designed for standard HTML file upload forms.

Form fields:
- file: The image file

Returns same response as /inline-images endpoint.

Hide (soft-delete/archive) an email message.

Unblock an email sender (remove from blacklist).

List all email connections for the tenant.

and email_integrations (Gmail, SMTP/IMAP, Proxy).

Each connection includes computed capabilities:

Returns the email connection that is configured as the active campaign provider.

Searches both email_provider_configs and email_integrations tables.

delete.description:
Delete an email connection.

Searches both email_provider_configs and email_integrations tables
and deletes the matching connection.

**WARNING:** This is a destructive operation. If you delete a campaign provider,
you will need to set a new one before sending campaigns.

patch.description:

Only connections with can_send_campaigns=True can be set as campaign providers
(SendGrid, Mailgun, SES).

This will unset any other campaign provider for the tenant.
Only one connection can be the campaign provider at a time.

**Required Scopes:** `email_integrations:update`

Link an outbound provider to a proxy integration.

This allows proxy integrations (which can receive inbound emails)
to send replies using a SendGrid, Mailgun, or SES provider.

Only proxy integrations can have linked outbound providers.

delete.description:
Unlink the outbound provider from a proxy integration.

After unlinking, the proxy integration will no longer be able to send replies.

**Required Scopes:** `email_integrations:update`

Returns aggregate statistics about unsubscribes for reporting/analytics.

- Contact provided updated email address

delete.description:
Delete custom role.

Add scopes to a custom role.

By default, only shows active (non-expired, non-revoked) tokens.

Create a new API token.

Save it securely - you won't be able to retrieve it again.

Token format: s7_api_<32_random_hex_chars>

get.description:

This endpoint expands wildcard scopes (*:*, resource:*, etc.) to show
all granular scopes the user can select when creating tokens.

Example:
- User has ['*:*'] -> Returns all 78 scopes
- User has ['campaigns:*'] -> Returns all campaigns:* scopes

This creates a new token string while keeping the same:
- Name
- Scopes
- Expiration date

The old token is immediately revoked.
IMPORTANT: Save the new token - it will only be shown once.

Read the persisted selective contact-sync filter. Returns the pre-feature
default (``mode = none`` — import everything) when nothing is stored yet.

Persist the selective contact-sync filter. The filter is VALIDATED against
HubSpot on save (a HubSpot 400 surfaces its own limit message); persisting
ALSO increments ``sync_generation`` so a sync run using the previous filter
self-interrupts. Narrowing stops adding non-matching contacts but does not
delete already-synced ones; widening does not auto-backfill (import is a

members, creates the list, subscribes them via the unified subscription
system) — the "migrate leads -> send campaign" flow.

field-mapping dropdown (replacing free-text property inputs). Each item:
``name``, ``label``, ``type``, ``field_type``, ``group_name``, ``custom``.

"Contact methods" and "Social media profiles" settings sections —
``{"contact_methods": [{"target": "email", "label": "Email (primary)"}, ...],
"social_profiles": [{"target": "linkedin", "label": "LinkedIn"}, ...]}``.

targets to build the ``contact_method_mapping`` sent to ``PATCH

property. If the connected portal did not grant it, this returns 400.

Create a SendSeven list whose membership is backed by a live HubSpot list.

post.description:
Create a new WhatsApp message template

**Required Scopes:** `channels:admin`

Submits a new template to Meta for approval. Templates typically take
24-48 hours to be reviewed and approved.

Template name must be lowercase, using only letters, numbers, and underscores.

Components structure:
- HEADER (optional): TEXT, IMAGE, VIDEO, or DOCUMENT
- BODY (required): Main message text with {{1}}, {{2}} placeholders
- FOOTER (optional): Small text at bottom
- BUTTONS (optional): Up to 3 buttons

Example:
```json
{
    "channel_id": "uuid",
    "name": "order_confirmation",
    "category": "UTILITY",
    "language": "en",
    "components": [
        {"type": "HEADER", "format": "TEXT", "text": "Order Update"},
        {"type": "BODY", "text": "Hi {{1}}, your order #{{2}} has been shipped!",
         "example": {"body_text": [["John", "12345"]]}},
        {"type": "FOOTER", "text": "Reply STOP to unsubscribe"},
        {"type": "BUTTONS", "buttons": [
            {"type": "URL", "text": "Track Order", "url": "https://example.com/track/{{1}}"}
        ]}
    ]
}
```

CAROUSEL templates carry their cards in a `CAROUSEL` component's `cards`
array (up to 10). Each card mirrors a mini-template — exactly one
IMAGE/VIDEO header, an OPTIONAL BODY, and a REQUIRED BUTTONS component with
1-2 buttons — and Meta requires every card to share the same header format,
the same body-presence, and an identical button layout. Those structural
rules are validated up front (400 on failure) before the template is
submitted to Meta; in particular a button-less card is caught here instead
of coming back from Meta as an unexplained "Invalid parameter".

AUTHENTICATION templates are not free-form: WhatsApp generates the message
text, so no HEADER and no BODY/FOOTER text are accepted. The only options
are `{"type": "BODY", "add_security_recommendation": true}`,
`{"type": "FOOTER", "code_expiration_minutes": 1..90}` and exactly one
`COPY_CODE` button (label max 25 chars; added as "Copy Code" when omitted),
plus the optional top-level `message_send_ttl_seconds` (30-900). Any other
component shape is rejected with an actionable 400 before Meta is called.

get.description:
Get WhatsApp messaging window status for a conversation

WhatsApp Business API restricts sending free-form messages outside a window
after the last customer message. This endpoint returns the current window
status so the UI can gate free-form vs template composition.

**Two window kinds:**
- `customer_service` (default): standard **24-hour** window measured from the
  last inbound customer message. Once expired only template messages may be
  sent (`requires_template` true).
- `free_entry_point`: a **72-hour** Free Entry Point (FEP) window for
  Click-to-WhatsApp / Page-CTA conversations (flagged at ingestion via
  `custom_data.ctwa.is_free_entry_point`). Per Meta, the FEP conversation
  "is opened as soon as your reply message is delivered and lasts 72 hours",
  so we anchor it at the **business's first outbound message after the
  referral** (the closest signal we have to delivery time). While open, any
  message type (free-form OR template) is allowed and is free.

**Important:** For fresh conversations where `last_customer_message_at` is null,
we check for recent inbound messages from the same contact on the same channel
(across all conversations) to determine the window status.

**Required Scopes:** `conversations:read`

Args:
    conversation_id: The conversation ID to check
    tenant_id: Tenant ID from authentication (automatic)

Returns:
    WhatsAppWindowStatusResponse (see schema): in_window, window_type,
    remaining_seconds, requires_template, is_free_entry_point,
    last_customer_message_at, window_end_at, free_entry_point_anchor_at.

Raises:
    404: Conversation not found or access denied

Whether an OUTBOUND WhatsApp call can be placed on this conversation now,
plus the call-permission window expiry (Feature #34 backend half).

Mirrors ``/conversations/{id}/whatsapp-window`` (the 24h MESSAGING window) but
for the CALL-permission window. WhatsApp's business-initiated calling requires
an open call-permission window — granted by the customer (a permission grant
or a prior connected call) and lasting **7 days (168h)**. The "Call" button in
the conversation view gates on this.

**What we can derive today (and the gaps):**
- ``calling_disabled``  — the master switch (``WHATSAPP_CALLING_ENABLED``) is
  off OR the channel's ``calling_enabled`` config flag is off. Hard block.
- ``no_permission``     — we have NO signal of a granted call-permission
  window: no prior CONNECTED (answered) call on this conversation. We anchor
  the window at the most recent answered call's ``answered_at`` + 7 days
  (the closest signal we persist). GAP: we do NOT yet persist Meta's explicit
  ``callback_permission_status`` grant/expiry per contact, so a permission
  granted WITHOUT a prior connected call is not reflected here — flagged for a
  follow-up (persist the grant from the calls webhook).
- ``calling`` allowed   — calling enabled AND a connected call within the last
  7 days → ``can_call: true`` with ``call_window_expires_at``.

Response (frontend contract):
  ``{ can_call: bool, call_window_expires_at: ISO8601|null, reason: str|null,
      billable: bool, last_connected_call_at: ISO8601|null }``
``reason`` ∈ {no_permission, opted_out, rate_limited, calling_disabled, null}.
Outbound is billable-on-answer, so ``billable`` is always true when
``can_call`` (the UI can color the button accordingly).

**Required Scopes:** `calls:view`

schema.title: Response Get Whatsapp Call Window Api V1 Whatsapp Conversations  Conversation Id  Call Window Get

put.description:
Update the user's mode + replace their per-inbox grants.

Behaviour:
- Validates target user is a member of this tenant (404 otherwise — using
  404 over 403 to avoid an existence oracle).
- Validates every ``inbox_ids`` element belongs to this tenant (422
  otherwise).
- Updates ``tenant_users.inbox_access_mode`` on PRIMARY.
- Reconciles the user's rows in ``custom_inbox_users`` on SHARD to the
  target set (delete grants no longer wanted, insert only missing ones).

Cross-DB write contract:
    The mode lives on PRIMARY; the grants live on SHARD. We cannot wrap
    both writes in a single transaction. Order is PRIMARY first, then
    SHARD. If the SHARD write fails AFTER the PRIMARY commit, the user is
    left with the new mode but stale grants — we log loudly and re-raise
    so the client sees the failure (and the frontend can avoid
    invalidating its cache, prompting the operator to retry). A retry of
    the same PUT is idempotent because PRIMARY will already be at the
    target value and the SHARD reconcile only touches the delta (a
    re-grant of an already-present inbox is a no-op, not a 1062 collision).

**Required Scopes:** ``team:update``

get.summary: List the tenant's configured SMS senders
get.description:
List every SMS sender configured for the tenant.

The frontend cannot get this from ``/channels``: ``ChannelResponse``
deliberately omits ``Channel.config`` (it holds API tokens and secrets),
so ``sender_type`` / ``mode`` / ``msisdn_or_alpha`` were invisible. This
endpoint returns a hand-whitelisted projection of those non-secret facts.
``seven_io_subaccount_id`` and every other credential stay server-side.

Inactive / archived senders ARE included so the UI can show them as
archived, but they are never ``is_default_for_send``.

Archived channels have ``config = None`` (``Channel.archive()`` calls
``_clear_credentials()``), so ``sender_type`` is recovered from the
``sms_phone_numbers.number_type`` row (which survives archiving) or from
the identifier shape. One case remains genuinely undecidable: an archived
row with no ``sms_phone_numbers`` row and a phone-shaped identifier, where
``dedicated`` and ``verified_own`` are indistinguishable. Those rows are
omitted (and logged) rather than guessed — ``pagination.total`` counts only
rows that are actually returned. Active channels always carry
``config["sender_type"]``, so a live sender can never be omitted.

``is_default_for_send`` marks the ONE sender an auto-selected send will
actually use. It comes from the same
:func:`app.services.sms.sender_identity.pick_default_sms_channel` helper
the send path in ``app/api/messages.py`` calls, so the badge is truthful
by construction rather than by convention.

**Required Scopes:** ``channels:read``

AttachmentFromUrlRequest.title: AttachmentFromUrlRequest
AttachmentFromUrlRequest.description:
Request body for POST /api/v1/attachments/from-url.

Fetches a remote URL server-side, validates the bytes against the
same MIME / size rules as POST /upload, stores them in our private
GCS bucket, and returns an attachment ID. Per-tenant URL dedup: the
same `url` will return the existing attachment without re-fetching.

download_url.title: Download Url
download_url.description: Authenticated proxy URL for downloading the attachment. Same-origin path (e.g. `/api/v1/attachments/{id}/download`) the browser fetches with the user's session cookie. The underlying GCS bucket is private; this is NOT a public URL. Use this for in-app render / agent UI / bot flows.

public_url.description: Absolute, **unauthenticated** public URL for the attachment (e.g. `https://api.sendseven.com/api/v1/attachments/public/{tenant_id}/{attachment_id}/{filename}`). Use this only for outbound contexts where an external service must `GET` the bytes — WhatsApp template `image.link` (Meta caches on first send), third-party webhook payloads, etc. The URL acts as a capability: anyone who has it can fetch the bytes. Don't put it in places that don't need it.

CarouselCardRequest.title: CarouselCardRequest
CarouselCardRequest.description:
A single carousel card within a CAROUSEL component.

A card mirrors a mini-template: its ``components`` list holds exactly one
HEADER (format IMAGE or VIDEO), exactly one BODY, and an optional BUTTONS
component. This is shape-only — structural rules (card count, header
format, cross-card consistency) are enforced at the route/service layer.

Security hardening (API DoS): the mutual recursion between this model and
``TemplateComponentRequest`` (``components`` -> ``cards`` -> ``components``)
is capped here fail-closed. An inner card component may ONLY be
HEADER/BODY/BUTTONS — never a nested CAROUSEL, and never carry its own
``cards`` — and each BODY is length-bounded. This runs as a ``mode="before"``
validator so a hostile deeply-nested payload is rejected BEFORE Pydantic
recurses into (and fully parses) the inner components.

ChannelChainEntry.title: ChannelChainEntry
ChannelChainEntry.description:
One entry in a Send node's ``channel_chain``.

The wire shape historically was ``list[str]`` — each item a channel
type ("whatsapp", "email", ...). It now widens to accept EITHER a
bare string OR an object pinning a specific Channel row::

    # Legacy bare-string form (still supported):
    ["whatsapp", "email"]

    # New object form — pin to a specific WhatsApp / Messenger page:
    [
      {"channel_type": "whatsapp", "channel_id": "<uuid>"},
      {"channel_type": "email"},  # channel_id null → tenant-default
    ]

Bare strings are normalized to ``ChannelChainEntry(channel_type=s,
channel_id=None)`` via ``normalize_channel_chain`` so service-layer
code (``send_node.py``, ``observability``, etc.) sees a single shape.

rcs_message_traffic_type.title: Rcs Message Traffic Type
rcs_message_traffic_type.description: [RCS] The channel's DEFAULT `messageTrafficType` (`AUTHENTICATION` | `TRANSACTION` | `PROMOTION` | `SERVICEREQUEST` | `ACKNOWLEDGEMENT`), or `null` when none is set. A German regulatory declaration about the nature of the message (UWG / telecoms), NOT a billing tier and not a delivery-speed setting. `null` means unset -- the adapter then falls back to `SERVICEREQUEST` -- and is what an archived channel reads, since this value is deliberately not preserved across archiving. Returned canonicalised, i.e. exactly the value that will be sent to Google; a stored value outside the five enum values reads as `null` because that is what the adapter will make of it. Set it with `PUT /channels/{id}/rcs/credentials`.

ChannelResponse.title: ChannelResponse
ChannelResponse.description:
Schema for channel response.

SECURITY: The 'config' field is intentionally excluded. It contains
API tokens, secrets, and credentials that must NEVER be returned via API.
Use 'identifier' for display purposes (phone number, bot username, page ID).

For WhatsApp channels:
- ``identifier`` returns a purely numeric phone number (no '+' or spaces)
- ``phone_number_formatted`` returns the human-readable formatted number

For RCS channels, three NON-SECRET columns are surfaced so the channel UI
can render the agent identity and the launch lifecycle straight off the
``GET /channels`` row. The two secret RCS columns
(``rcs_service_account_json`` -- one key that can send as ANY of our
agents -- and ``rcs_client_token``) are deliberately absent and MUST NEVER
be added here or to any other read schema.

``rcs_message_traffic_type`` is the ONE ``config`` key this schema exposes,
and it arrives via the ``Channel.rcs_message_traffic_type`` **property** --
not by relaxing the config exclusion. Do not "simplify" that into returning
``config`` (or a filtered copy of it): the exclusion above is the reason a
rotated ``access_token`` has never come back out of this endpoint, and a
passthrough is how the next new secret key would.

definition.title: Definition
definition.description: The full flow graph: ``trigger`` + ``nodes[]`` + ``edges[]`` + ``entry_node_id``. See ``fl01_create_flows.py`` migration docstring for the locked JSON shape. Hard-capped at 256 KB JSON-encoded; validated against the structural rules in ``FlowDefinitionValidator``.

re_entry_policy.title: Re Entry Policy
re_entry_policy.description: How to behave when the same contact is triggered again while a run is already in flight. MVP only enforces ``block`` (ignore the new trigger). ``restart`` and ``parallel`` are scaffolded for Phase 3 UX.

default_language.title: Default Language
default_language.description: Per-flow fallback language used by the runtime when a contact has no resolvable locale. Typically set by the frontend to the operator's current UI language at create time. Backend defaults to ``'en'`` (DB server_default) if omitted. Must be one of the curated ~40 ``SUPPORTED_TRANSLATION_LOCALES``.

manually_triggerable.title: Manually Triggerable
manually_triggerable.description: When True, the flow appears in the operator's manual-start picker and accepts ``POST /flows/{id}/runs`` requests. Automatically forced True when the trigger kind is ``manual``.

auto_translate_messages.title: Auto Translate Messages
auto_translate_messages.description: Per-flow opt-in for runtime LLM translation of outbound Send-node messages into the contact's preferred language.

language_detection_strategy.title: Language Detection Strategy
language_detection_strategy.description: How this flow's runs resolve the language they speak to a contact. ``cascade`` (the default) resolves per run via the fallback chain (contact locale → inferred channel locale → ``default_language``). ``fixed`` always speaks ``default_language``, skipping the cascade. OMIT / ``null`` to keep the default — NULL is stored and treated as ``cascade`` by the runtime, so existing flows are unaffected. Any value other than ``cascade`` / ``fixed`` is rejected with 422.

default_channel_chain.title: Default Channel Chain
default_channel_chain.description: Flow-level channel fallback chain — May 2026 this is the SINGLE source of truth for channel order (per-node ``channel_chain`` has been removed; node configs only carry content). Bare channel-type strings (``["whatsapp", "live_chat"]``) OR ``{channel_type, channel_id?}`` objects pinning a specific Channel row. When omitted / NULL on create, the server seeds from the tenant's active channels in a sensible order. A flow with any send/choice/collect_input node MUST have a non-empty chain to validate.

stop_on_agent_reply.title: Stop On Agent Reply
stop_on_agent_reply.description: When True (the default), the flow engine terminates any active run for the contact + conversation the moment a human agent sends an outbound message. Bot replies and flow-Send messages do NOT trip the hook — only operator-authored outbound messages do. Set to False for long-running drips whose cadence should be independent of agent activity.

stop_on_conversation_closed.title: Stop On Conversation Closed
stop_on_conversation_closed.description: When True (the default), the flow engine terminates any active run scoped to the conversation the moment that conversation is closed. Only runs whose recorded ``context.conversation_id`` matches the closed conversation are canceled — flows without a recorded conversation are left untouched. Set to False for long-running re-engagement drips that intentionally outlive the original conversation.

priority.title: Priority
priority.description: Trigger-arbitration priority among INBOUND-EVENT-triggered (entry) flows. LOWER = higher priority (evaluated FIRST). When multiple entry flows match the same inbound event they start in ascending-priority order. Default 0. Background flows (manual/api_event/schedule) ignore this field.

exclusive.title: Exclusive
exclusive.description: When True, while a run of this entry-triggered flow is actively running on a conversation, NO other entry-triggered flow may start on that conversation (background manual/api/schedule flows are exempt). Default False preserves today's fire-all behaviour.

channel_id.title: Channel Id
channel_id.description: Pinned channel UUID — REQUIRED for chat-app channel types (whatsapp, telegram, sms, messenger, instagram, rcs). The channel IS the sender for these. Must be NULL for ``channel_type=email`` (use ``email_mailbox_id`` instead).

email_mailbox_id.title: Email Mailbox Id
email_mailbox_id.description: Pinned EmailMailbox UUID — REQUIRED for ``channel_type=email``. The mailbox is the sender (controls the From: address). Must be NULL for chat-app channel types.

payload.title: Payload
payload.description: Free-form JSON payload. Same per-channel rules as ``scheduled_sends.payload``: WhatsApp REQUIRES ``{template_id, variables}``; email accepts EITHER free-text (``{subject, text|html}``) OR templated (``{template_id, variables?}``) — mutually exclusive; SMS/Telegram/Messenger/Instagram/RCS must NOT carry ``template_id`` but MAY carry ``attachments`` (a list of ≤20 attachment UUIDs owned by your workspace). Hard-capped at 64 KB.

time_of_day_local.title: Time Of Day Local
time_of_day_local.description: Local clock time as "HH:MM" or "HH:MM:SS". Required for `birthday` rules. Optional for `recurring_cron` (the RRULE controls timing). Ignored for `segment_blast`.

timezone.title: Timezone
timezone.description: IANA tz name (e.g. ``Europe/Berlin``). NULL semantics: birthday → contact-local TZ, recurring_cron/segment_blast → UTC.

recurrence_rule.title: Recurrence Rule
recurrence_rule.description: iCalendar RRULE string. Required for `recurring_cron`; must be NULL for `birthday` and `segment_blast`.

segment_filter.title: Segment Filter
segment_filter.description:
Audience selector. Two accepted shapes:
  * NEW: ``{"match_op": "any"|"all", "rules": [{"kind": "tag"|"list"|"language", "op": ..., "values": [...]}]}``
  * LEGACY: ``{"tags": [...], "tags_op": "any"|"all"}`` (normalized by the engine).
NULL for `birthday` (audience is implicit).

next_evaluation_at.title: Next Evaluation At
next_evaluation_at.description: For `segment_blast`: the dispatch time. For other kinds the evaluator manages this cursor — leaving it NULL is fine.

contact_id.title: Contact Id
contact_id.description: Contact UUID on the tenant's shard

channel_id.title: Channel Id
channel_id.description: Pinned channel UUID — REQUIRED for chat-app channel types (whatsapp, telegram, sms, messenger, instagram, rcs). Each chat-app channel IS the sender (for RCS: the RBM agent). Leave NULL only for ``channel_type=email`` (use ``email_mailbox_id`` instead).

email_mailbox_id.title: Email Mailbox Id
email_mailbox_id.description: Pinned EmailMailbox UUID — REQUIRED for ``channel_type=email``. The mailbox is the sender (controls the From: address and the underlying provider/integration). Must be NULL for chat-app channel types (use ``channel_id`` instead).

payload.title: Payload
payload.description:
Free-form JSON payload. Per-channel rules:
  - WhatsApp: REQUIRES ``{template_id, variables}`` — free text is rejected because the 24h messaging window cannot be guaranteed at schedule time.
  - Email: EITHER ``{subject, text|html, include_signature?}`` (free-text) OR ``{template_id, variables?}`` (references an EmailContent template). Mutually exclusive.
  - SMS / Telegram / Messenger / Instagram / RCS: rendered text payload (e.g. ``{"text": "..."}``), optionally with ``attachments`` — a list of attachment UUIDs (uploaded via ``POST /attachments/upload``) fanned out as one message per attachment at fire time. Max 20. Every id must belong to your workspace.
Hard-capped at 64 KB JSON-encoded.

send_at.title: Send At
send_at.description: First-fire timestamp (timezone-aware UTC). Must be at least 1 minute in the future.

recurrence_rule.title: Recurrence Rule
recurrence_rule.description: Optional iCalendar RRULE (e.g. ``FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=9``). When set, the row stays in ``scheduled`` after firing and ``next_run_at`` advances per the rule. Capped at 255 chars.

timezone.title: Timezone
timezone.description: IANA timezone for recurrence interpretation (e.g. ``Europe/Berlin``). Defaults to UTC. Currently informational; recurrence math runs in UTC so this is preserved for display only.

language.description: ISO language code (e.g., en, de, es)

allow_category_change.description: Allow Meta to change template category if needed

parameter_format.title: Parameter Format
parameter_format.description: Placeholder style for the template body. `positional` uses `{{1}}`, `{{2}}`, ...; `named` uses identifier placeholders like `{{first_name}}`. When `named`, supply `body_named_examples` instead of `example.body_text` on the BODY component.

Only meaningful for DOCUMENT header templates.

EmailContentCreate.title: EmailContentCreate
EmailContentCreate.description:
Schema for creating email content with variable system.

Supports two content types:
- **html** (default): Full MJML content with visual editor support
- **plain_text**: Plain text template with {{variable}} placeholders

The variable system supports 4 types of variables:
1. Template variables: Custom content (e.g., {{hero_title}}, {{cta_url}})
   - Filled via variable_values field or form mode
2. Contact variables: Auto-filled from contact data (e.g., {{contact.name}})
   - Replaced at send time with actual contact data
3. Company variables: Auto-filled from company data (e.g., {{company.name}})
   - Replaced at send time with company info
4. System variables: Auto-filled by platform (e.g., {{system.year}})
   - Replaced at send time with system values

Variable naming convention: lowercase_with_underscores
Examples: hero_title, contact.name (valid), heroTitle, hero-title (invalid)

source.description: 'api' when a user started it, 'enqueue' when re-created mid-chain

FAQMigrationRunInfo.title: FAQMigrationRunInfo
FAQMigrationRunInfo.description:
The in-flight marker for a migration.

Held in Redis with a TTL and refreshed on every enqueue, so it exists for
as long as the self-re-enqueueing chain does. It can be absent while a
migration is genuinely running (Redis unavailable) — which is why
`running` is not derived from it alone.

dry_run.title: Dry Run
dry_run.description: Preview only. Runs INLINE (no job is enqueued, no LLM call, no row written) and returns the clustering it would have processed

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: Cap on summaries read in one pass (default: all, max 20000)

max_clusters.title: Max Clusters
max_clusters.description: Clusters processed per worker message (default 40). Higher values risk the 600s worker message timeout; the job re-enqueues itself either way, so raising this buys nothing but risk

min_cluster_size.title: Min Cluster Size
min_cluster_size.description: Override the tenant's `faq_min_cluster_size` for this run — the floor at which a cluster counts as recurring rather than one-off

include_singletons.title: Include Singletons
include_singletons.description: Process one-off cases too. Set false for the cheap high-value pass: singletons dominate the cluster count and the cost, and are refused almost every time

retire_folder_when_done.title: Retire Folder When Done
retire_folder_when_done.description: Hide the legacy 'Ticket Summaries' KB folder once nothing is left to migrate. A visible change to the tenant's KB tree, so opt-in. Ignored for `dry_run`

force.title: Force
force.description: Start even though a migration appears to be in flight, overriding the 409. Only for a run known to be dead — two live chains double-bill the tenant and race on the same summaries

FAQMigrationStartRequest.title: FAQMigrationStartRequest
FAQMigrationStartRequest.description: Parameters for one migration run (or preview).

status.title: Status
status.description: 'queued' — a job was published; 'preview' — dry run, nothing enqueued

run_id.title: Run Id
run_id.description: Null for a preview (a preview is not a run)

forced.title: Forced
forced.description: True when the in-flight guard was explicitly overridden

lease_held.title: Lease Held
lease_held.description: Whether the in-flight marker was actually stored. False means Redis was unavailable and duplicate-start protection falls back to the database activity check alone

running.title: Running
running.description: INFERRED, not recorded: true when the in-flight marker exists, or when the migration wrote a row in the last few minutes while work remains. See `running_evidence`

run.description: The in-flight marker, when one exists

summaries_total.title: Summaries Total
summaries_total.description: Distinct conversations with a summary the migration can read. Marginally optimistic: a run also drops records with empty intent text and caps itself at 20000

summaries_migrated.title: Summaries Migrated
summaries_migrated.description: Distinct conversation ids recorded as consumed by migrated rows

percent_summaries_processed.title: Percent Summaries Processed
percent_summaries_processed.description: summaries_migrated / summaries_total * 100, rounded to 1 decimal. This is the ONLY progress ratio the backend can substantiate — it measures summaries consumed, NOT clusters done and NOT time elapsed, and it moves in jumps of a whole cluster. Null when the tenant has no summaries. There is no cluster-level or ETA progress record; ask `?include_estimate=true` (or /faq-migration/estimate) for a fresh cluster count

entries_imported.title: Entries Imported
entries_imported.description: FAQ entries the migration created (drafts, unless later changed)

entries_by_status.title: Entries By Status
entries_by_status.description: Imported entries grouped by current status (draft/published/...)

clusters_rejected.title: Clusters Rejected
clusters_rejected.description: Clusters consumed without producing an entry — refused as non-reusable, blocked for PII, or merged into an existing entry. Stored as ARCHIVED ledger rows

last_activity_at.title: Last Activity At
last_activity_at.description: Newest migrated row — the migration's real heartbeat

estimate.description: Fresh clustering pass. Only present with `?include_estimate=true` — it re-clusters the whole pending corpus, so do not poll with it

FAQMigrationStatusResponse.description:

FlowOptAction.title: FlowOptAction
FlowOptAction.description:
Opt-in / opt-out action that STARTS A FLOW.

`flow_id` is a LOGICAL reference to a same-shard `flows.id` — there is NO
DB foreign key (an FK can't live in a JSON column and config must not
cascade-delete a flow); the service validates existence + same-tenant.

occurred_at.title: Occurred At
occurred_at.description: Chronological anchor (``flow_runs.started_at``). Used as the merge sort key.

current_node_label.title: Current Node Label
current_node_label.description: Human-readable label of the current node, resolved from ``flow_runs.context.definition_snapshot.nodes[node_id].label``. Falls back to ``current_node_id`` when no label is present in the snapshot.

wait.description: The soonest-expiring active wait for this run — populated only when status == waiting.

messages_count.title: Messages Count
messages_count.description: Number of messages attributed to this flow_run (``messages.flow_run_id == flow_run_id``).

error_message.title: Error Message
error_message.description: Run-level failure summary mirrored from ``flow_runs.context.last_error``. ``None`` for successful or in-flight runs.

failed_node_id.title: Failed Node Id
failed_node_id.description: Node where the engine gave up. Mirrors the run-detail endpoint's field.

failed_node_label.title: Failed Node Label
failed_node_label.description: Human label for ``failed_node_id``, resolved from the same snapshot used by ``current_node_label``.

FlowRunEvent.title: FlowRunEvent
FlowRunEvent.description: Timeline row representing a single flow run for the contact.

items.title: Items
items.description: Messages attributed to the flow run, oldest-first

FlowRunMessageListResponse.title: FlowRunMessageListResponse
FlowRunMessageListResponse.description: Paginated flow-run transcript — same envelope as ``MessageListResponse``.

conversation_id.title: Conversation Id
conversation_id.description: Conversation the message belongs to. Null for flow messages that were sent before any conversation existed (e.g. test runs, or runs the contact never replied to).

contact_info.title: Contact Info
contact_info.description: Provider-echoed sender profile captured from the inbound channel webhook at receipt time (inbound message.received only; not a DB lookup). Fields vary by channel: WhatsApp {name, phone}, Telegram {name, username, profile_picture}, Messenger {name, profile_picture}, Instagram {name?, username, profile_picture}. NOTE: `phone` (WhatsApp-only) is deprecated — use `data.contact_method.value` for the authoritative DB-sourced identifier of the method actually used.

related_message_ids.title: Related Message Ids
related_message_ids.description: IDs of the additional messages created by the same send request, in delivery order. Non-empty only when a send carried several attachments on a channel that delivers one attachment per message — the response body itself is the FIRST message (it holds the caption and `attachments[0]`), and each id here is a further message carrying the next attachment. Each has its own status and its own delivery webhooks, so poll them individually via `GET /api/v1/messages/{id}`. Empty array for every other message.

content_format.title: Content Format
content_format.description: How this message's body is formatted for the send pipeline: `markdown` (canonical markdown, rendered per-channel) or `plain` (human text, passed through untouched). Derived from `meta.content_format`; defaults to `plain` for every message that did not explicitly opt into markdown.

interactive.description: Interactive message content (WhatsApp-style Meta format) for messages with reply buttons or a list. Hydrated from `meta.interactive`. Null for non-interactive/legacy messages.

header_media_url.title: Header Media Url
header_media_url.description: Resolved media URL for an interactive image/video header

header_media_attachment_id.title: Header Media Attachment Id
header_media_attachment_id.description: Durable attachment id for an interactive image/video header

reply_to_external_id.title: Reply To External Id
reply_to_external_id.description: Platform message ID of quoted message

campaign.description: Campaign info when this message was sent via a campaign/newsletter

flow_run_id.title: Flow Run Id
flow_run_id.description: FlowRun UUID — set when this message was sent by an automation flow. Frontends use this (together with `flow_name`) to render a 'Sent by flow' badge in the conversation timeline.

flow_step_id.title: Flow Step Id
flow_step_id.description: FlowRunStep UUID — identifies the specific Send-node step inside the flow that produced this message. Optional companion to `flow_run_id`.

flow_name.title: Flow Name
flow_name.description: Display name of the flow that sent this message. NOT stored on the message row — populated by the API layer via a single batch lookup against `flow_runs JOIN flows` and only set when `flow_run_id` is non-null.

edited_at.title: Edited At
edited_at.description: When this message was last edited by the sender (real column on `messages`, stamped when an edit event is applied). Non-null is the ONLY signal that a message was edited — `text` is silently replaced in place, so without this a client cannot tell an edited message from an original one. Null for every message that was never edited (the overwhelming majority).

previous_text.title: Previous Text
previous_text.description: Body this message had immediately BEFORE its most recent edit. Not stored on the message row — resolved by the API layer from the newest APPLIED `message_revisions` row in one batched lookup per page. Null means 'edited, but the superseded body is unknown': most edits arrive before/without the message they target, so the original body was often never captured. Clients must therefore treat null as valid and fall back to a plain non-interactive 'edited' marker instead of an edit-history UI.

revision_count.title: Revision Count
revision_count.description: Number of edits that have actually been APPLIED to this message. Pending revisions (an edit whose target message we never resolved) are deliberately excluded — they describe no visible change to this row. 0 for un-edited messages; a value >1 tells the client the body was edited repeatedly, so `previous_text` is only the last step of a longer history.

FlowRunMessageResponse.title: FlowRunMessageResponse
FlowRunMessageResponse.description:
``MessageResponse`` variant for the flow-run transcript endpoint
(``GET /flows/{flow_id}/runs/{run_id}/messages``).

Flow Send-node messages are persisted BEFORE any conversation exists
(``messages.conversation_id`` was relaxed to NULL in ``fl06``; the
messages_in_worker backfill stitches them into the contact's first
inbound reply later). Test runs and runs that never got a reply keep
``conversation_id = NULL`` forever, which the public ``MessageResponse``
originally rejected (``conversation_id: str``) — Sentry BACKEND-8Y. The
base ``MessageResponse.conversation_id`` is now itself ``Optional[str]``
(campaign mirror messages hit the same case); this subclass keeps its
flow-specific field description and remains the endpoint's response model.

FlowRunResponse.title: FlowRunResponse
FlowRunResponse.description:
Wire format for a FlowRun row.

The ``error_message`` / ``failed_node_id`` / ``failed_node_label`` fields
are derived by the API layer (see ``_to_run_response``) — they are not
stored on the ``flow_runs`` row directly. ``error_message`` mirrors
``context.last_error``; ``failed_node_id`` is the node where the engine
gave up (resolved from ``current_node_id`` or the last failed
``flow_run_steps`` row); ``failed_node_label`` is the human label for
that node, looked up against the current ``flows.definition``.

FlowRunStatus.title: FlowRunStatus
FlowRunStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a flow run.

Lowercase values to match the MySQL ENUM (see fl02 migration).
``values_callable`` is set on the SQLAlchemy column so the lowercase
values are written/read correctly.

FlowRunStepListResponse.title: FlowRunStepListResponse
FlowRunStepListResponse.description: Paginated list of FlowRunSteps (run audit trail).

node_label.title: Node Label
node_label.description: Human-readable label for the node, looked up in the current ``flows.definition`` (``display_name`` → snapshot ``label``/``name`` → derived from ``node_type`` + config).

node_config_snapshot.title: Node Config Snapshot
node_config_snapshot.description: Subset of the node's CURRENT config from ``flows.definition`` (not a point-in-time snapshot of what the engine executed). Surfaced fields are node-type specific (e.g. ``validation``, ``max_attempts``, ``on_timeout_node_id``, ``prompt`` for Collect Input). ``None`` when the node no longer exists in the flow definition.

branch_taken.title: Branch Taken
branch_taken.description: Branch label the engine routed to from this node, when applicable. Derived from ``output_snapshot.chosen_branch``.

FlowRunStepResponse.title: FlowRunStepResponse
FlowRunStepResponse.description:
Wire format for a FlowRunStep row (audit trail entry).

``node_label`` and ``node_config_snapshot`` are derived by the API
layer from the CURRENT ``flows.definition`` (we don't freeze per-step
config snapshots in the audit table). For a published-then-edited
flow, the config returned here is the latest authored config, not
the config the engine executed against — callers that need
point-in-time fidelity should use ``input_snapshot``, which the
engine populates from the per-run ``definition_snapshot``.

``branch_taken`` is best-effort: derived from
``output_snapshot.chosen_branch`` for branching node types (choice /
collect_input). ``None`` for nodes that don't branch.

expires_at.title: Expires At
expires_at.description: When this wait will fire / time out (UTC). NULL for waits that have no timeout.

event_key.title: Event Key
event_key.description: Wait resolution key — e.g. 'reply:WHATSAPP' or 'event:contact.created'. NULL for timers.

FlowRunWaitSummary.title: FlowRunWaitSummary
FlowRunWaitSummary.description:
Compact summary of the wait a flow_run is parked on.

Populated only when ``FlowRunEvent.status == "waiting"``. The picker
in :mod:`app.services.contact_history_service` selects the
soonest-expiring wait per run (so the FE can render "Waiting until
2026-05-20 14:00" without inspecting every wait row).

FlowScreenInfo.title: FlowScreenInfo
FlowScreenInfo.description: Information about a screen in a flow

preview.title: Preview
preview.description: Masked hint: first 3 + last 2 chars, or *** for short values

FlowSecretEntry.title: FlowSecretEntry
FlowSecretEntry.description: One secret as listed — the value is write-only and never returned.

FlowStatus.title: FlowStatus
FlowStatus.description:
Flow lifecycle status.

Lowercase values to match the MySQL ENUM (see fl01_create_flows
migration). values_callable is set on the SQLAlchemy column so the
lowercase values are written/read correctly.

FlowValidationError.title: FlowValidationError
FlowValidationError.description:
One structured publish-time validation error.

``path`` is a best-effort dotted/bracketed locator (e.g.
``"nodes[sales_bot].bot_id"`` or ``"trigger.recurrence_rule"``) so
the Flows editor can highlight the offending node / trigger inline
without re-running save-then-fail. Graph-level errors (orphan
node, unreachable from entry, cycle) carry ``path=""`` and the
human-readable message stays in ``message``.

FlowValidationStatus.title: FlowValidationStatus
FlowValidationStatus.description:
Publish-time validation snapshot embedded in FlowResponse.

``can_activate`` mirrors the result of
``FlowDefinitionValidator.validate_publish`` — when False the FE
should gate the "Publish" / "Activate" button and surface
``errors`` inline. Save-time leniency (placeholder ``bot_id`` on a
template-just-imported flow) means a flow may exist with
``can_activate=false`` and still be a valid draft.

FlowVariableEntry.title: FlowVariableEntry
FlowVariableEntry.description:
One row in the Flow Builder's Branch-node variable picker.

* ``path``  — the canonical reference the Branch node expression
  evaluates (e.g. ``"contact.first_name"``, ``"contact.custom.vip"``,
  or a flow-scoped ``output_var`` like ``"flow.vars.user_email"``).
* ``label`` — human-readable name shown in the picker dropdown.
* ``type``  — best-effort type hint (e.g. ``"string"``, ``"number"``,
  ``"string[]"``). Used by the FE to pick the right operator set.

FlowVariablesResponse.title: FlowVariablesResponse
FlowVariablesResponse.description:
Catalog payload for ``GET /flows/variables``.

Used by the Branch node's "match contact field / tag / list / custom
field" UI to render a typed picker instead of a free-text input.

Sections:

* ``contact_fields``  — built-in Contact columns (first/last name,
  email, phone, language, country, tags, lists).
* ``custom_fields``   — tenant-specific custom field definitions
  (``contact.custom.<slug>`` paths).
* ``tags``            — tenant tags (``path=name``, ``label=name``).
* ``lists``           — tenant subscription lists (``path=list_id``,
  ``label=list_name``).
* ``flow_variables``  — when the ``flow_id`` query param is supplied,
  the names produced by the flow's ``collect_input`` /
  ``create_tracked_link`` / ``kb_query`` nodes
  (``flow.vars.<output_var_name>``).

folder_id.description: ID of the folder queued for deletion

queued_documents.title: Queued Documents
queued_documents.description: Number of contained documents also queued for deletion

HubSpotContactSyncFilterModel.title: HubSpotContactSyncFilterModel
HubSpotContactSyncFilterModel.description:
The persisted selective-sync config (GET/PUT /contact-sync-filter),
stored verbatim in ``HubSpotConnection.contact_sync_filter_config``.

``mode`` picks which sub-object is authoritative: ``properties``
(filter_groups), ``list`` (a single HubSpot list), or ``none`` (import
everything — the pre-feature default). ``updated_at`` / ``updated_by_user_id``
are server-populated on PUT and echoed on GET (they live INSIDE the JSON

InvitationRoleEnum.title: InvitationRoleEnum
InvitationRoleEnum.description:
Allowed invitation roles - maps to RBAC system roles.

There are exactly 7 system roles (migration 059, Jan 2026, consolidated the
original 10 and renamed them SCREAMING_SNAKE -> display case). The slugs below
map onto them in ``app/api/invitations.py::role_mapping``:

- OWNER            -> "Owner"          Full access to everything (*:*)
- ADMIN            -> "Admin"          Full access EXCEPT billing (zero billing scopes)
- SUPPORT_AGENT    -> "Support Agent"  Conversations, tickets, contacts, knowledge base
- MARKETING_AGENT  -> "Marketing"      Campaigns, email, lists, contacts
- VIEWER           -> "Viewer"         Read-only access to all resources
- BILLING_ADMIN    -> "Billing"        Billing management only
- DEVELOPER        -> "Developer"      API tokens, webhooks, technical settings

ANALYST, CONTENT_MANAGER and DESIGNER are RETIRED roles. They are kept in this
enum only so old pending invitations still resolve, and they fold onto a
surviving role (analyst/designer -> Viewer, content_manager -> Marketing).
Do NOT offer them in new UI or docs.

New integrations should pass ``role_id`` (an RBAC Role UUID from ``GET /roles``)
instead of a slug -- that path also supports tenant-created custom roles.

reply_to_message_id.title: Reply To Message Id
reply_to_message_id.description: Optional UUID of a prior message in the SAME conversation to reply to (threaded / quote reply). The target message must already have a platform external_id; the outbound message is sent as a native quote-reply on channels that support it (WhatsApp, Telegram, Instagram, Live Chat). Rejected with 4xx if the target is not found in this conversation or has no external_id yet.

subject.title: Subject
subject.description: Email subject line — REQUIRED for email channel sends, ignored for chat-app channels (whatsapp/telegram/sms/etc.). When omitted for an email reply, the conversation's existing subject is used (prefixed with 'Re: ' if not already). The API rejects an email send with no resolvable subject (SendGrid 400s on empty subject).

attachments.title: Attachments
attachments.description:
Attachment IDs (UUIDs) returned from POST /api/v1/attachments/upload or POST /api/v1/attachments/from-url. Do NOT pass raw URLs here — fetch them via /attachments/from-url first to get an ID.

Accepts either an array or a single bare ID string (`"<uuid>"` is treated as `["<uuid>"]`). Whitespace is trimmed and empty entries are dropped.

On channels that can only carry ONE media object per message (WhatsApp, Telegram, Messenger, Instagram, SMS/MMS, browser push, RCS) several attachments are delivered as several messages — one per attachment, with `text` used as the caption of the FIRST one. This response returns the first message; the additional ones are listed in `related_message_ids`. Email (MIME parts) and live chat deliver all attachments inside a single message.

attachment_filenames.title: Attachment Filenames
attachment_filenames.description: Optional per-message display-filename overrides for `attachments`, aligned positionally by index (entry N overrides the filename of `attachments[N]`). Controls the filename shown to the recipient — e.g. Meta's `filename` field on a WhatsApp document, so the user sees `Invoice-2026.pdf` instead of the stored object name. When omitted (or an entry is null/empty), the send path falls back to the original filename stored on the Attachment record (`attachments.filename`). If the list is shorter than `attachments`, only the leading attachments are overridden; extra entries beyond the number of attachments are ignored. Every entry now takes effect: on a channel that delivers one attachment per message, entry N is the filename of the message carrying `attachments[N]`.

is_voice.title: Is Voice
is_voice.description: Mark this message as a voice message (push-to-talk). Only valid when `message_type` is `audio` AND at least one attachment (the recorded audio) is supplied — the server rejects the send (422) otherwise. When true, `duration_ms` is required. Persisted into the message's `meta` as `meta.is_voice` (sibling meta keys are preserved). The recorded file is the first entry in `attachments` (a normal Attachment ID); the messages-out worker transcodes it to OGG/Opus before delivery. Default false → ordinary audio file send (unchanged behavior).

duration_ms.title: Duration Ms
duration_ms.description: Recorded duration of the voice message in milliseconds. REQUIRED when `is_voice` is true; must be > 0 and <= 300000 (5 minutes — longer recordings are rejected with 422). Ignored when `is_voice` is false. Persisted into `meta.duration_ms`.

include_signature.title: Include Signature
include_signature.description: Append the sender's email signature to outbound email (EmailSignature for the user, falling back to EmailSignatureTemplate for the tenant). Default `true` for email; ignored for chat-app channels.

sender_id.title: Sender Id
sender_id.description: Optional sender override for email channel sends. The id either of an EmailIntegration (proxy / gmail / smtp-imap / ses-managed) or an EmailProviderConfig (SendGrid / Mailgun / SES). Surface candidates via GET /api/v1/conversations/{id}/sender-options. The server validates the choice against the user's EmailMailbox ACL, additionally allowing the conversation's default reply sender (the receiving connection's outbound_provider) even when the user is not on that mailbox's ACL. Ignored for non-email channels.

message_traffic_type.title: Message Traffic Type
message_traffic_type.description: RCS only. Declares the traffic class of this send to the mobile carrier (`AgentMessage.messageTrafficType`): one of `AUTHENTICATION`, `TRANSACTION`, `PROMOTION`, `SERVICEREQUEST`, `ACKNOWLEDGEMENT`. This is a REGULATORY declaration, not a billing option — if the message is marketing you must declare `PROMOTION`. Omitted (the default) means `SERVICEREQUEST`, which is correct only for replies to a customer's own enquiry. Unrecognised values are ignored (the default applies) rather than failing the send. Ignored by all non-RCS channels.

content_format.title: Content Format
content_format.description: How the send pipeline must treat the message body. `plain` (the default when omitted) = human-typed text, passed through to the channel UNTOUCHED. `markdown` = canonical markdown that the channel adapter renders into each channel's own formatting. Omit this for normal human replies — only AI/bot/flow-generated content should opt into `markdown`. Stored on the message as `meta.content_format`; absence is always treated as `plain`.

content.description: DEPRECATED: use text and message_type directly

MessageCreate.title: MessageCreate
MessageCreate.description:
Schema for creating/sending a new message.

Supports 3 resolution modes:

**Mode 1: conversation_id only** (reply to existing conversation)
- Provide just `conversation_id` and `text`. The recipient (`to`) is automatically
  resolved from the conversation's contact method or last inbound message.
- Example: ``{"conversation_id": "...", "text": "Hello!"}``

**Mode 2: contact_method_id** (cleanest, resolves everything)
- Provide `contact_method_id` and `text`. The `to`, `channel_id`, and `contact_id`
  are all resolved from the contact method record.
- Example: ``{"contact_method_id": "...", "text": "Hello!"}``

**Mode 3: contact_id + optional to + channel_id** (explicit, auto-creates contact_method)
- Provide `contact_id` (and optionally `to` and `channel_id`). The conversation is
  auto-resolved from the contact. A contact_method is auto-created if one doesn't exist.
- Example: ``{"contact_id": "...", "to": "+49...", "text": "Hello!"}``

Fields:
- to: Recipient external ID (phone, telegram_id, etc.) - optional when conversation_id
  or contact_method_id is provided
- conversation_id: Optional, conversation to send in (auto-resolved if not provided)
- contact_method_id: Optional, cleanest way to send - resolves to, channel_id, and
  contact_id automatically
- contact_id: Optional, used to auto-resolve conversation when conversation_id is omitted
- channel_id: Optional, used when creating a new conversation or for ambiguous recipients
- message_type: Optional, defaults to "text"
- text: Message content
- attachments: Optional list of attachment IDs
- meta: Optional customer-defined metadata

Estimated retail price for an outbound SMS.

Used by the frontend to show "this campaign will cost ~X EUR" before
the customer clicks Send. ``platform_fee_eur`` is seven.io's per-segment
cost (min across networks for the destination country); ``sendseven_fee_eur``
is our flat margin on top. ``total_per_segment_eur`` = platform + margin
and is also returned as the legacy ``price_per_message_eur`` field for
backward compatibility with older frontend builds.

When a ``text`` is supplied, the response also includes the segment
count (GSM-7 vs UCS-2) and the projected total cost.

conversation_id.title: Conversation Id
conversation_id.description: Conversation the message belongs to. May be null for campaign and flow messages sent to a contact that has no conversation on that channel (campaigns never create conversations; flow messages are attached once the contact replies).

contact_info.title: Contact Info
contact_info.description: Provider-echoed sender profile captured from the inbound channel webhook at receipt time (inbound message.received only; not a DB lookup). Fields vary by channel: WhatsApp {name, phone}, Telegram {name, username, profile_picture}, Messenger {name, profile_picture}, Instagram {name?, username, profile_picture}. NOTE: `phone` (WhatsApp-only) is deprecated — use `data.contact_method.value` for the authoritative DB-sourced identifier of the method actually used.

related_message_ids.title: Related Message Ids
related_message_ids.description: IDs of the additional messages created by the same send request, in delivery order. Non-empty only when a send carried several attachments on a channel that delivers one attachment per message — the response body itself is the FIRST message (it holds the caption and `attachments[0]`), and each id here is a further message carrying the next attachment. Each has its own status and its own delivery webhooks, so poll them individually via `GET /api/v1/messages/{id}`. Empty array for every other message.

content_format.title: Content Format
content_format.description: How this message's body is formatted for the send pipeline: `markdown` (canonical markdown, rendered per-channel) or `plain` (human text, passed through untouched). Derived from `meta.content_format`; defaults to `plain` for every message that did not explicitly opt into markdown.

interactive.description: Interactive message content (WhatsApp-style Meta format) for messages with reply buttons or a list. Hydrated from `meta.interactive`. Null for non-interactive/legacy messages.

header_media_url.title: Header Media Url
header_media_url.description: Resolved media URL for an interactive image/video header

header_media_attachment_id.title: Header Media Attachment Id
header_media_attachment_id.description: Durable attachment id for an interactive image/video header

reply_to_external_id.title: Reply To External Id
reply_to_external_id.description: Platform message ID of quoted message

campaign.description: Campaign info when this message was sent via a campaign/newsletter

flow_run_id.title: Flow Run Id
flow_run_id.description: FlowRun UUID — set when this message was sent by an automation flow. Frontends use this (together with `flow_name`) to render a 'Sent by flow' badge in the conversation timeline.

flow_step_id.title: Flow Step Id
flow_step_id.description: FlowRunStep UUID — identifies the specific Send-node step inside the flow that produced this message. Optional companion to `flow_run_id`.

flow_name.title: Flow Name
flow_name.description: Display name of the flow that sent this message. NOT stored on the message row — populated by the API layer via a single batch lookup against `flow_runs JOIN flows` and only set when `flow_run_id` is non-null.

edited_at.title: Edited At
edited_at.description: When this message was last edited by the sender (real column on `messages`, stamped when an edit event is applied). Non-null is the ONLY signal that a message was edited — `text` is silently replaced in place, so without this a client cannot tell an edited message from an original one. Null for every message that was never edited (the overwhelming majority).

previous_text.title: Previous Text
previous_text.description: Body this message had immediately BEFORE its most recent edit. Not stored on the message row — resolved by the API layer from the newest APPLIED `message_revisions` row in one batched lookup per page. Null means 'edited, but the superseded body is unknown': most edits arrive before/without the message they target, so the original body was often never captured. Clients must therefore treat null as valid and fall back to a plain non-interactive 'edited' marker instead of an edit-history UI.

revision_count.title: Revision Count
revision_count.description: Number of edits that have actually been APPLIED to this message. Pending revisions (an edit whose target message we never resolved) are deliberately excluded — they describe no visible change to this row. 0 for un-edited messages; a value >1 tells the client the body was edited repeatedly, so `previous_text` is only the last step of a longer history.

MUST stay in lockstep with ``app.models.message.MessageType`` AND the
MySQL ENUM column ``messages.message_type``. Validation here is what
gates the API response — any value the DB column accepts MUST be a
member of this enum, or ``MessageResponse.model_validate`` raises
``ValidationError`` and the whole list endpoint 500s. Bug found
2026-05-30: prod conversations carrying ``button`` rows from a
template-quick-reply click crashed ``GET /api/v1/messages``.

Interactive message types:
- quick_reply: Cross-platform quick reply buttons (Messenger, Instagram, Telegram)
- interactive: WhatsApp interactive messages (buttons/lists)
- carousel: Multi-card carousel messages
- button: WhatsApp legacy template-button reply (callback button payload)

Adapter-level types:
- file: Generic file attachment fallback (Messenger/Instagram unknown content_type)
- reaction: Emoji reaction (merged into target message metadata)
- referral: Messenger m.me deep link / ad referral event

Worker-emitted types:
- whatsapp_template: Campaign-dispatched WhatsApp template message
- kb_response: Team-chat AI knowledge-base response
- notification: System notification message

OpenOrCreateConversationRequest.title: OpenOrCreateConversationRequest
OpenOrCreateConversationRequest.description:
Request to open an existing conversation or create a new one.

This is a simplified endpoint that does NOT send a message.
Use this when you want to navigate to a conversation and compose
messages using the normal chat UI.

For email channels, use `use_conversation_id` to specify which existing
thread to use instead of creating a new one.

**Two-phase API usage:**
1. First call `/conversations/check-existing` to see if open/closed conversations exist
2. Then call this endpoint with `action` to specify what to do:
   - `action="create_new"`: Always create a new conversation (fires webhook)
   - `action="reopen_existing"`: Reopen closed conversation (fires conversation.reopened webhook)
   - `action="auto"` (default): Backwards compatible behavior

PreviousConversationsResponse.title: PreviousConversationsResponse

Aggregate summary of a contact's previous conversations.

Redesigned (June 2026) to power a single-line history summary plus the
reopen-&-merge affordance, instead of a list of heavy per-conversation
cards. The expensive per-item enrichment (bulk message counts,
last-message previews, channel-type hydration) is NO LONGER computed —
`items` is retained for backwards-compatibility but is returned EMPTY.
Consumers that want the actual messages should use
`GET /api/v1/contacts/{contact_id}/messages`.

All aggregate fields respect the SAME contact-history visibility scoping
as the merge gating, so a non-admin agent never sees counts/targets for
channels they cannot access.

url.title: Url
url.description: Destination for a `url` button. Must be an absolute **https** URL. Required when `type` is `url`, and rejected otherwise.

action.title: Action
action.description: What a `postback` button does. `start_flow` starts the flow named by `flow_id` when the recipient taps the button. Omit for a plain opaque `payload`. Implied when `flow_id` is set.

flow_id.title: Flow Id
flow_id.description: The flow to start, when `action` is `start_flow`. Must be a published flow in this workspace. A flow whose trigger is "Comment received" cannot be used here — that trigger is reserved for the first message and its private reply has already been spent on the message carrying this button.

payload.description: Opaque value echoed back to you when a `postback` button is tapped. It arrives on the resulting inbound message as `meta.button_id`. Defaults to `title` when omitted. Cannot be combined with `action`/`flow_id`, and cannot start with the reserved `flow_start:` prefix.

attachment_id.description: Editor-side hint on a `url` button whose URL is an attachment's public link ("file button"). Stored so an editor can re-open the button as a file; never sent to the recipient. The link is not reference-counted — deleting the attachment later breaks it.

PrivateReplyButton.title: PrivateReplyButton
PrivateReplyButton.description:
One button in a private reply. Supported on Facebook Messenger and
Instagram alike (verified on live accounts).

Two kinds, distinguished by `type`:

* `url` — opens a web page. Requires `url`. Nothing comes back to you.
* `postback` (the default) — sends a value back to you on tap. Either set
  `action: "start_flow"` + `flow_id` to start one of your flows, or set an
  opaque `payload` you match yourself.

conversation_id.title: Conversation Id
conversation_id.description: Conversation the reply was filed into — open this to continue the DM.

status.title: Status
status.description: Delivery status of the reply message.

sent_by_user_id.title: Sent By User Id
sent_by_user_id.description: The agent who sent it. Null when an automation did (see `source`).

created_at.title: Created At

sent_at.title: Sent At
sent_at.description: When the reply was accepted by Meta.

PrivateReplyMessageRef.title: PrivateReplyMessageRef
PrivateReplyMessageRef.description:
The outbound private reply that answered a comment.

This is the **comment → message** half of the reply linkage. It carries
enough to render a preview next to the comment and to deep-link into the
conversation, without a second round trip.

content_type.title: Content Type
content_type.description: Meta's chip kind. Only `text` is supported. Optional — Meta's own documented payload includes it, so it is accepted verbatim.

action.title: Action
action.description: Set to `start_flow` (with `flow_id`) to start a flow when the chip is tapped. Implied when `flow_id` is set. Omit for a plain opaque `payload`.

flow_id.title: Flow Id
flow_id.description: The flow to start, when `action` is `start_flow`. Must be a published flow in this workspace, and must NOT use the "Comment received" trigger — that trigger answers the comment itself, and this comment's one allowed private reply is the message carrying this chip.

payload.title: Payload
payload.description: Opaque value echoed back on tap, as `meta.button_id`. Defaults to `title` when omitted. Cannot be combined with `action`/`flow_id`, and cannot start with the reserved `flow_start:` prefix.

PrivateReplyQuickReply.title: PrivateReplyQuickReply
PrivateReplyQuickReply.description:
One quick reply chip in a private reply. Supported on Facebook
Messenger and Instagram alike.

Meta allows up to 13 chips and they ride ALONGSIDE the message, so quick
replies may be combined with `text`, with `image_url`, or with `buttons` —
a button template is just the attachment the chips accompany.

Like a button, a chip can start one of your flows: set
`action: "start_flow"` + `flow_id`. A tapped chip reaches the same handler
a tapped button does, because Meta reports it as `message.quick_reply` and
we normalise that to the same `meta.button_id` field.

text.title: Text
text.description: The message body — or the button template's body when `buttons` is set.

channel_id.title: Channel Id
channel_id.description: The Instagram or Facebook Messenger channel whose post was commented on. RcsCapabilityResponse.description:
Per-recipient reachability for THIS agent.

``reachable: false`` is an ANSWER, not an error. RBM returns 404 for every
kind of unreachable — no RCS on the device, RCS switched off, a carrier the
agent is not launched on, or a tester who has not accepted the invite yet —
and it cannot tell them apart. So the endpoint returns 200 with
``reachable: false`` and a coarse ``reason``; inventing a specific cause
would be a guess presented as a fact.

RcsContent.title: RcsContent
RcsContent.description:
RCS for Business (Google RBM) campaign content.

Note what is NOT here: RBM has no template approval and no 24-hour
re-engagement window, so none of the WhatsApp template fields transfer —
there is no template id/name/language/category and no variable_mapping.
Content is composed freely.

``message_traffic_type`` is also deliberately absent. It is a German carrier
/regulatory declaration about the nature of the message (UWG §7), and the
campaigns worker always declares ``PROMOTION`` for Reach traffic; a
per-campaign override would let marketing be declared as transactional.

Bounds are enforced by ``RcsAdapter`` rather than repeated here, so this
schema cannot drift from the platform: text is auto-split at 3072 chars, the
whole AgentMessage is capped at 250 KB, suggestions at 11 per message but 4
per card with 25-char labels and 2048-char postbackData, and carousels must
hold 2–10 cards.

When False (default), the re-crawl is non-destructive: existing documents are updated in-place and orphaned documents are cleaned up only after a successful crawl (crawl-then-reconcile).

RecrawlRequest.title: RecrawlRequest
RecrawlRequest.description:
Request model for re-crawling a previously crawled domain.

Supports two modes:
- "existing_pages": Re-crawl the exact URLs from previous crawl history (faster, predictable)
- "full_rescan": Re-discover pages via sitemap/BFS from scratch (finds new pages, more thorough)

Both modes use non-destructive crawl-then-reconcile: existing documents are updated in-place,
new documents are created, and orphaned documents (not touched by this crawl) are removed
only after the crawl completes successfully.

* ``flow_ids``: an ordered list of flow ids. The server assigns

must be unique within the request.
