SegmentCondition.title: SegmentCondition
SegmentCondition.description:
Schema for a single segment condition.

Used in dynamic lists to filter contacts based on field values.

**Available filter fields:**

- ``contact_method``: Unified contact-method filter evaluated against the
  ``contact_methods`` table. Parameters:

  - ``method_type`` (required): one of ``whatsapp_id``, ``telegram_id``,
    ``email``, ``phone``, ``messenger_id``, ``instagram_id``.
  - ``operator``: ``has`` / ``not_has`` (presence checks), or ``equals`` /
    ``contains`` (value matches, requires ``value``).
  - ``value``: string to match (only for ``equals`` / ``contains``).
  - ``channel_id`` (optional UUID): only meaningful for the page-scoped
    types ``messenger_id`` / ``instagram_id``; ignored for global types.
  - ``phone_type`` (optional, e.g. ``mobile``): only meaningful for
    ``phone``.

  Value matching normalizes the input the same way the write path does
  (digits-only for phone-shaped types, lowercase for email), so saved
  filters reliably match stored rows.
- ``name``: Contact name filter (operators: equals, contains).
- ``email``, ``phone``: Contact field filters (operators: equals, contains).
  These now evaluate against the ``contact_methods`` table (matching across
  all of a contact's methods, not just the denormalized primary), so a
  contact with a non-primary matching email/phone is now included.
- ``custom_field``: Custom field filter (requires ``key``; operators: equals, contains, gt, gte, lt, lte).
- ``has_tag`` / ``not_has_tag``: Tag membership (value = tag UUID).
- ``has_telegram``, ``has_whatsapp``, ``has_messenger``, ``has_instagram``:
  Retained legacy aliases for boolean channel-presence checks
  (operator: equals, value: true/false). Prefer ``contact_method`` with
  ``operator=has``/``not_has`` for new filters.
- ``has_optin``: Subscription/opt-in check via ``contact_subscriptions``.
  Extra parameters: ``list_id`` (optional UUID), ``channel_type`` (optional; any
  ``SubscriptionChannelType`` value — see the field description for the live list),
  ``require_confirmed`` (optional bool).
  When ``value`` is true, matches contacts WITH a matching subscription; when false, matches
  contacts WITHOUT one.
- ``not_has_optin``: Alias that negates ``has_optin`` (value=true means no subscription).

Reserved dict keys (`url_suffix`, `otp_code`, and their indexed variants) apply per card.

Accepts the same forms as the top-level `header_media_url` (bare attachment id, proxy URL, permanent public URL, legacy GCS URL, or an external https URL). Each carousel card has its own header media, so supply one per card.

SendTemplateCardParams.title: SendTemplateCardParams
SendTemplateCardParams.description:
Per-card send parameters for a CAROUSEL template.

Supplied positionally in ``SendTemplateRequest.cards`` — index 0 fills the
first card, index 1 the second, and so on. Each card's ``variable_values``
follows the SAME positional/named rules (and reserved-key handling) as the
top-level body ``variable_values``, resolved against that card's own body
placeholders. This is the template-send INPUT shape; the service maps it
onto the unified carousel content representation before dispatch.

contact_id.title: Contact Id
contact_id.description: Contact to send the message to. OPTIONAL — supply ANY ONE of `contact_id`, `contact_method_id`, `conversation_id`, or `whatsapp_id` to identify the recipient. If `contact_method_id` is also provided it WINS and this `contact_id` is ignored. When combined with `whatsapp_id`, this contact is used (and a matching WhatsApp contact method is auto-created on it if missing).

contact_method_id.title: Contact Method Id
contact_method_id.description: OPTIONAL. A `contact_methods.id` (UUID) of type `whatsapp_id` or `whatsapp_bsuid` owned by the tenant. When provided it determines BOTH the recipient WhatsApp id (the method's value) AND the contact (the method's owning contact). Highest-priority recipient selector — if both `contact_id` and `contact_method_id` are given, `contact_method_id` WINS and `contact_id` is ignored. A method of any other type returns 422.

whatsapp_id.title: Whatsapp Id
whatsapp_id.description: OPTIONAL. A WhatsApp recipient id sent directly — a phone number WITHOUT a leading `+` (a leading `+` is stripped; spaces/dashes/parens are tolerated for phone-shaped values), an alphanumeric WhatsApp id (Meta now permits alphanumeric ids — digits are NOT required), OR a Business-scoped user ID such as `US.13491208655302741918` (kept verbatim, periods included, and sent in Meta's `recipient` field instead of `to`). The value is normalized with the same canonical contact-method normalization used elsewhere so dedup is consistent. If `contact_id` is also supplied, that contact gains a `whatsapp_id` (or `whatsapp_bsuid`) method with this value (created if missing); otherwise an existing contact is matched by this identifier, or a new contact + method is created. Note that AUTHENTICATION templates cannot be sent to a Business-scoped user ID (Meta error 131062). When sent without a `conversation_id`, the new conversation's channel is the template's channel (optionally selected via `channel_id`).

channel_id.title: Channel Id
channel_id.description: OPTIONAL. A WhatsApp channel id (UUID) owned by the tenant. Always allowed alongside any recipient selector. Used to (a) disambiguate a template referenced by NAME that exists on multiple channels, and (b) select the sending channel when sending by `whatsapp_id` with no contact/conversation. If it conflicts with the resolved template's own channel, the request returns 400.

variable_values.title: Variable Values
variable_values.description:
Override auto-mapped values. Pass a list (positional only) or a dict (positional with numeric keys, or named with identifier keys). Shape must match the template's parameter_format.

Reserved dict keys (coexist with body variable keys):
- `url_suffix` — replaces `{{1}}` inside a dynamic URL button. Value is ONLY the suffix portion that fills `{{1}}`, not the full URL (e.g. for template URL `https://example.com/orders/{{1}}`, pass `"url_suffix": "track/INV-2026-001"`).
- `otp_code` — the code copied by the user for authentication / OTP COPY_CODE buttons.

language.title: Language
language.description:
OPTIONAL. Template language to send when the template is referenced BY NAME and that name exists in multiple languages. Use the exact code stored in `whatsapp_templates.language` — the Meta language/locale code (e.g. `en`, `de`, `en_US`, `pt_BR`).

Resolution when a name maps to multiple language rows (after the channel filter): if only one language remains it is used; if several remain, an explicit `language` selects that variant (400 if no such variant), else the recipient contact's stored `language` is matched (exact, then base-language family e.g. `de_DE`↔`de`), else 400 asking for `language`. When the template is referenced by DB ID the language is fixed by that row; passing a conflicting `language` returns 400.

conversation_id.description: Link to existing conversation (creates new if not provided)

header_media_url.title: Header Media Url
header_media_url.description:
Header media reference for IMAGE/VIDEO/DOCUMENT templates. Accepts ANY of:
- a bare `attachment_id` (UUID) returned by `POST /attachments` or `POST /whatsapp-templates/upload-media`
- the proxy URL `/api/v1/attachments/{id}/download` (relative or absolute)
- the permanent public URL `/api/v1/attachments/public/{tenant_id}/{id}`
- a legacy `https://storage.googleapis.com/...` GCS URL
- any absolute external `https://` URL (customer CDN, etc.)

The server resolves the input to a Meta-deliverable URL via `WhatsAppHeaderMediaService`. Field name is kept for backwards compatibility — it has not been URL-only since May 2026.

cards.title: Cards
cards.description: Per-card parameters for a CAROUSEL template, supplied POSITIONALLY — entry 0 fills the first card, entry 1 the second, etc. Provide one entry per card you want to personalize. When ABSENT the non-carousel send path is unchanged. Each entry carries its own `variable_values` (same positional/named rules as the top-level field) and `header_media_url`. Only meaningful for CAROUSEL templates; ignored otherwise.

SendTemplateRequest.title: SendTemplateRequest
SendTemplateRequest.description:
Request to send a template message.

``variable_values`` accepts EITHER a list (positional templates) OR a dict
(positional with numeric keys, or named with identifier keys). The accepted
shape is determined by the template's ``parameter_format``:

* ``positional`` template → ``["John", "ORD-98765"]`` or
  ``{"1": "John", "2": "ORD-98765"}``.
* ``named`` template → ``{"first_name": "John", "order_id": "ORD-98765"}``.

Sending the wrong shape returns 400 with an actionable error. Order in the
NAMED dict is irrelevant — Meta resolves by ``parameter_name``.

Reserved keys in ``variable_values`` (only valid when passed as a dict;
they coexist with the regular body variable keys ``"1"``, ``"2"``, ... or
named identifiers):

* ``url_suffix`` — replaces the ``{{1}}`` placeholder inside a dynamic URL
  button (e.g. template URL ``https://example.com/orders/{{1}}``). Pass
  ONLY the suffix portion that fills ``{{1}}``, not the full URL. This
  key targets button index 0; use the indexed form below to address
  additional dynamic URL buttons on the same template.
* ``url_suffix_<button_index>`` — same as ``url_suffix`` but addresses a
  specific button by its 0-based index in the template's ``BUTTONS``
  component (e.g. ``url_suffix_1`` for the second button). When both
  ``url_suffix`` and ``url_suffix_0`` are present, the indexed form wins.
* ``otp_code`` — the code value for an authentication / OTP COPY_CODE
  button. This is the string the user copies when tapping the button.
* ``otp_code_<button_index>`` — indexed variant for templates with more
  than one COPY_CODE button. Same precedence rules as ``url_suffix_*``.

``app/schemas/channel.py`` deliberately excludes ``Channel.config``
because it holds API tokens, secrets and credentials that must NEVER be
returned via the API. This schema exists so the frontend can see the few
non-secret SMS facts it needs (``sender_type``, ``mode``,
``msisdn_or_alpha``) WITHOUT that ban being relaxed. Every field below is
named explicitly — the endpoint never dumps ``config``, and in particular
never exposes ``seven_io_subaccount_id``. Do not add a passthrough field.

snoozed_until.title: Snoozed Until
snoozed_until.description: Timezone-aware ISO datetime when the snooze should expire. Must be in the future. After this moment the conversation behaves as a normal open conversation again.

reopen_on_message.title: Reopen On Message
reopen_on_message.description: When true, an inbound customer message arriving while the conversation is snoozed clears the snooze and returns it to the Open tab (handled by the inbound-message worker).

SnoozeConversationRequest.title: SnoozeConversationRequest
SnoozeConversationRequest.description:
Request body for snoozing (postponing) a conversation.

Snooze is a derived state: the conversation status remains ``open`` while
snoozed; it is hidden from the Open tab and surfaced on the Snoozed tab
until ``snoozed_until`` passes (query-time expiry, no background job).

items.title: Items
items.description: List of items for this page

updated_at.title: Updated At
updated_at.description: When the resource was last updated (UTC)

social_post_id.title: Social Post Id
social_post_id.description: Our id for the post it was left on.

channel_id.title: Channel Id
channel_id.description: Channel the post belongs to.

external_comment_id.title: External Comment Id
external_comment_id.description: Meta's comment id. **This is the value to pass to `POST /comments/{comment_id}/private-reply`**, and the value that appears on the reply message as `meta.comment_id`.

parent_external_comment_id.title: Parent External Comment Id
parent_external_comment_id.description: Meta's id of the comment this one replies to. Null for a top-level comment.

is_reply.title: Is Reply
is_reply.description: True when this comment is a threaded reply to another comment (`parent_external_comment_id` is set).

author_external_id.title: Author External Id
author_external_id.description: The commenter's platform-scoped id (Instagram IGSID / Facebook PSID).

author_username.title: Author Username
author_username.description: The commenter's username/handle, when Meta supplied one.

is_from_owner.title: Is From Owner
is_from_owner.description: True when the comment is from the connected account itself — most often our own public reply, which Meta echoes back as an ordinary comment. Such comments never count as unanswered and are hidden from listings unless `include_owner=true`.

contact_id.title: Contact Id
contact_id.description: The commenter as a contact in your workspace. Null until they are resolved — which happens the first time we message them.

text.title: Text
text.description: The comment text. Null for a media-only comment.

attachment_url.title: Attachment Url
attachment_url.description: URL of the comment's media, for a photo/sticker/video comment (these carry no text). A Facebook feature — Instagram comments cannot contain media. May be a signed CDN URL that expires.

attachment_type.title: Attachment Type
attachment_type.description: Kind of `attachment_url`: `image` (photos and stickers) or `video`. Null when the comment has no media.

state.title: State
state.description: `pending` (unanswered) · `auto_replied` (a rule or flow answered it) · `replied` (an agent answered it) · `handled` (cleared without a private reply) · `ignored` (our own comment, or dismissed).

commented_at.title: Commented At
commented_at.description: Meta's timestamp for the comment — the business time.

replied_at.title: Replied At
replied_at.description: When the private reply was sent.

replied_by_user_id.title: Replied By User Id
replied_by_user_id.description: The agent who replied, or who marked the comment handled. Null for an automated reply and for API-token callers.

handled_at.title: Handled At
handled_at.description: When the comment was marked handled or ignored.

private_reply_window_expires_at.title: Private Reply Window Expires At
private_reply_window_expires_at.description: End of Meta's 7-day private-reply window, measured from `commented_at`. Null when Meta gave no reliable comment timestamp.

private_reply_available.title: Private Reply Available
private_reply_available.description: Whether a private reply can still be sent right now. **False is the normal end state of most comments**, not an error — see `private_reply_unavailable_reason` for which one applies.

private_reply_unavailable_reason.title: Private Reply Unavailable Reason
private_reply_unavailable_reason.description:
Why `private_reply_available` is false, so the UI can say it rather than just grey out a button:

* `already_replied` — a private reply was already sent. Meta permits exactly one per comment, **forever**. Permanent.
* `window_expired` — the 7-day window closed. Permanent.
* `window_unknown` — Meta gave no reliable comment timestamp, so we cannot prove the window is open; we fail closed rather than offer a reply that Meta would reject.
* `marked_handled` — an agent cleared it without replying. Reversible: reopen it with `PATCH /comments/{comment_id}`.
* `ignored` — our own comment, or dismissed by a rule. Also reversible.

Null when a private reply IS available.

private_reply_message_id.title: Private Reply Message Id
private_reply_message_id.description: `messages.id` of the private reply that answered this comment — the link from a comment to its reply. Set for a reply we sent ourselves; null for a flow hand-off, where the flow's Send node owns the outbound message.

private_reply.description: The reply message itself, hydrated for rendering. Omitted when `include_reply=false`, and null when the message row is gone — message retention can outrun comment retention, and the comment must keep saying it WAS answered.

public_reply_id.title: Public Reply Id
public_reply_id.description: Meta's comment id of our public reply, when one was posted. Reserved: public replies are not part of the current release.

post.description: The post this comment was left on. Included where the caller has no post context (the cross-post inbox, and a single comment); omitted from the per-post thread, where it would repeat.

SocialCommentResponse.title: SocialCommentResponse
SocialCommentResponse.description:
One comment plus everything the UI needs to render its row.

Deliberately answers three questions a list row has to answer on its own:
*what was said*, *what state is it in*, and *can I still privately reply —
and if not, why not*.

SocialCommentRuleAction.title: SocialCommentRuleAction
SocialCommentRuleAction.description:
What a matching rule does. Exactly two options, on purpose.

``send_private_reply`` — the 90% case: one static (variable-substituted)
DM. Text-only, because Meta's private-reply API is text-only.

``start_flow`` — the escape hatch for "one entry message, then wait for the
user's answer". Hands off to the existing flow engine rather than growing a
second conversation runtime inside the rules engine.

type.title: Type
type.description: `url` opens a link; `postback` sends a value back to you.

url.title: Url
url.description: Destination of a `url` button. Absolute **https** URL, required for that type and rejected on a `postback` button.

action.title: Action
action.description: What a `postback` button does. `start_flow` starts `flow_id` for the person who tapped. Implied when `flow_id` is set.

flow_id.title: Flow Id
flow_id.description: Flow started by a `start_flow` button. Must be published and in this workspace, and must NOT be a "Comment received" flow — that trigger is reserved for the first message, whose one allowed private reply is the message carrying this button.

payload.title: Payload
payload.description: Opaque value returned to you on tap (as `meta.button_id`). Defaults to the label. Mutually exclusive with `action`/`flow_id`.

attachment_id.title: Attachment Id
attachment_id.description: Editor-side hint on a `url` button whose URL is an attachment's public link ("file button"). Stored so the editor can re-open the button as a file; never sent to the recipient. The link is not reference-counted — deleting the attachment later breaks it.

source.title: Source
source.description: Editor-side hint naming where a `url` button's link came from (e.g. `attachment`). Stored, never sent to the recipient.

SocialCommentRuleButton.title: SocialCommentRuleButton
SocialCommentRuleButton.description:
One button on a rule's private reply.

Shape-only validation lives here (enum membership, lengths). Everything
needing the database or the channel — "is this an Instagram channel?",
"does this flow exist in this tenant and can it be started from a button?"
— is enforced by ``private_reply_buttons.validate_and_normalize_buttons``
in the service layer, which is the SAME validator the manual
``POST /comments/{id}/private-reply`` endpoint runs. There is exactly one
set of button rules in the product.

name.title: Name
name.description: Operator-facing label, e.g. "Summer sale — send the code".

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Disabled rules are skipped entirely during evaluation.

priority.title: Priority
priority.description: Evaluation order — LOWER runs FIRST (same convention as flows). The first matching rule wins; no further rule is evaluated. Ties are broken by specificity (a post-scoped, keyworded rule beats a catch-all), then by age.

post_scope.description: Watch every post on the channel, or only selected posts.

post_ids.title: Post Ids
post_ids.description: Post identifiers to watch when post_scope is specific_posts. These are the platform's own post ids as returned by the channel's posts/media listing endpoint.

match_mode.description: any_comment reacts to every comment (no keywords needed, and it also matches comments with no text at all). contains / exact / starts_with compare against the keyword list, case-insensitively.

keywords.title: Keywords
keywords.description: Keywords to match. Ignored when match_mode is any_comment.

action.description: Send a private reply, or hand the comment off to a flow.

reply_text.title: Reply Text
reply_text.description: The private reply to send. Supports the same {{placeholders}} as the flow Send node — for example {{contact.first_name}} — plus {{comment.text}}, {{comment.author}} and {{post.caption}}.

flow_id.title: Flow Id
flow_id.description: Flow to start when action is start_flow. The flow's trigger must be "Comment received".

post_message_overrides.title: Post Message Overrides
post_message_overrides.description: Optional per-post wording: {post_id: message}. A post listed here gets that message instead of reply_text; every other post falls back to reply_text.

reply_buttons.title: Reply Buttons
reply_buttons.description: Up to 3 buttons attached to the private reply. Supported on both Facebook Messenger and Instagram. A control the rule's channel cannot carry is rejected when the rule is saved, not silently stripped when it fires. Only meaningful when action is send_private_reply.

reply_quick_replies.title: Reply Quick Replies
reply_quick_replies.description: DEPRECATED / IGNORED. Comment private replies are buttons-only since 2026-08-13. This field is still accepted for backwards compatibility so older clients do not get a 422, but it is never validated, stored, or sent — use reply_buttons instead.

channel_id.title: Channel Id
channel_id.description: The Instagram or Facebook channel this rule watches.

SocialCommentRuleCreate.title: SocialCommentRuleCreate
SocialCommentRuleCreate.description: POST body. ``channel_id`` is immutable, so it only exists here.

SocialCommentRuleMatchMode.title: SocialCommentRuleMatchMode
SocialCommentRuleMatchMode.description:
How ``keywords`` are compared against the comment text.

``contains`` / ``exact`` / ``starts_with`` are the EXACT modes
``match_comment_trigger`` already implements (case-insensitive, trimmed).
``any_comment`` is the "reply to everything" option: it needs no keywords
and matches even a text-less (image / sticker) comment.

SocialCommentRulePostScope.title: SocialCommentRulePostScope
SocialCommentRulePostScope.description:
Which posts a rule watches. Stored LOWERCASE (values_callable).

Values are IDENTICAL to the ``scope`` values of the ``comment_received``
flow trigger config so a rule can be handed to ``match_comment_trigger``
verbatim.

content_type.title: Content Type
content_type.description: Meta's chip kind. Only `text` is supported; the field exists so Meta's own documented payload validates unchanged.

title.title: Title
title.description: Chip label (Meta limit: 20 characters, truncated beyond that).

action.title: Action
action.description: What the chip does. `start_flow` starts `flow_id` for the person who tapped. Implied when `flow_id` is set.

flow_id.title: Flow Id
flow_id.description: Flow started by a `start_flow` chip. Must be published and in this workspace, and must NOT be a "Comment received" flow — that trigger is reserved for the first message, whose one allowed private reply is the message carrying this chip.

payload.title: Payload
payload.description: Opaque value returned to you on tap (as `meta.button_id`). Defaults to the label. Mutually exclusive with `action`/`flow_id`.

SocialCommentRuleQuickReply.title: SocialCommentRuleQuickReply
SocialCommentRuleQuickReply.description:
One quick-reply chip on a rule's private reply.

The sibling of :class:`SocialCommentRuleButton`, and the same division of
labour: shape-only validation here, everything needing the database or the
channel in ``private_reply_buttons.validate_and_normalize_quick_replies``
— the SAME validator the manual endpoint runs.

Differs from a button exactly where Meta differs: 13 permitted instead of
3, a `content_type` instead of a `type`, and **no URL kind** (Meta's quick
reply object has no URL variant). A chip that starts a flow behaves
identically to a button that starts a flow, including the ban on
"Comment received" flows.

SocialCommentRuleUpdate.title: SocialCommentRuleUpdate
SocialCommentRuleUpdate.description:
PATCH body — every field optional.

Deliberately NOT a subclass of the base: inheriting would drag the base's
defaults in, and a default is indistinguishable from an omitted field in a
PATCH. Here, "absent" genuinely means "leave it alone" (the endpoint uses
``exclude_unset``), so a caller can toggle ``enabled`` without restating the
rule. ``channel_id`` is absent on purpose: moving a rule to another channel
silently changes which posts it can match, so that is a delete + create.

state.title: State
state.description:
The new state:

* `handled` — you answered publicly or off-platform. Clears it from the unanswered queue.
* `ignored` — not actionable; skip it.
* `pending` — reopen a comment that was marked handled or ignored by mistake.

`replied` and `auto_replied` are **not** settable here: they mean a private reply message exists, and are set by actually sending one.

SocialCommentTriageRequest.title: SocialCommentTriageRequest
SocialCommentTriageRequest.description: Body of `PATCH /comments/{comment_id}` — clear a comment by hand.

SocialInsightsMetrics.title: SocialInsightsMetrics
SocialInsightsMetrics.description:
Platform-agnostic metric snapshot. A `null` field means the platform (or
this object type) does NOT expose that metric — it is never fabricated.

Instagram media exposes reach + engagement (`total_interactions`) + likes /
comments / shares / saves, but NOT `impressions` on the current API. A
Facebook post/page exposes reach + impressions + engagement via `/insights`;
per-post likes/comments/shares come from a different edge and stay `null` in
Phase 1.

channel_id.title: Channel Id
channel_id.description: The channel this target published to.

object_id.title: Object Id
object_id.description: Meta's id read (IG media id / FB `{page}_{post}`).

authorized.title: Authorized
authorized.description: False when the connection lacks the insights permission — the frontend should prompt a reconnect. See `error_code`.

error_code.title: Error Code
error_code.description: `insights_not_authorized` (reconnect to grant insights), `insights_unavailable` (Meta has no insights for this object), `insights_unsupported_platform`, or `insights_error`. Null on success.

last_refreshed_at.title: Last Refreshed At
last_refreshed_at.description: When this target's cached numbers were last refreshed from Meta. Null if this target has never been cached.

SocialInsightsTarget.title: SocialInsightsTarget
SocialInsightsTarget.description: Insights for one published target (one channel) of an authored post.

authorized.title: Authorized
authorized.description: False when the connection lacks the insights permission — the frontend should prompt a reconnect. See `error_code`.

error_code.title: Error Code
error_code.description: `insights_not_authorized` (reconnect to grant insights), `insights_unavailable` (Meta has no insights for this object), `insights_unsupported_platform` (channel is not IG/FB), or `insights_error`. Null on success / before any refresh.

last_refreshed_at.title: Last Refreshed At
last_refreshed_at.description: When these numbers were last refreshed from Meta. Null if this post's insights have never been refreshed (metrics are then null except the public-counter fallback for likes/comments).

SocialPostInsights.title: SocialPostInsights
SocialPostInsights.description:
Cached Meta insights for one comment-synced post (the Posts-LIST view).

FLAT by design: the Posts list renders each metric as its own cell, so the
nine metrics sit at the top level rather than under a nested ``metrics``
object (this differs from the authored-post ``SocialInsightsTarget`` in
``schemas/social_post.py``, which groups them under ``metrics``). Every
metric is ``int | null`` — ``null`` means Meta (or this object type) does
not expose that metric, or it has not been fetched yet; a metric is never
fabricated from a different one.

Served from the ``social_posts.insights_*`` cache columns — the LIST endpoint
makes NO live Graph call on load. ``likes`` / ``comments`` fall back to the
post's public counters (``like_count`` / ``comments_count``) when the richer
insights value has not been cached yet, so the list shows a number before the
first insights refresh; a refreshed insights value always wins over the
public counter.

items.title: Items
items.description: One entry per refreshed post, most recent first.

SocialPostInsightsBulkRefreshResponse.title: SocialPostInsightsBulkRefreshResponse
SocialPostInsightsBulkRefreshResponse.description:
`POST /comments/posts/insights/refresh` — bulk refresh outcome.

Refreshes the tenant's most-recent posts (bounded by ``limit``) to avoid a
Graph storm, and returns each refreshed post with its updated insights.

insights.description: The freshly-refreshed (and re-cached) insights for the post.

last_refreshed_at.title: Last Refreshed At
last_refreshed_at.description: The most recent ``insights_refreshed_at`` across the tenant's posts — how fresh the freshest number in this summary is. Null when no post has ever been refreshed.

SocialPostInsightsSummaryResponse.title: SocialPostInsightsSummaryResponse
SocialPostInsightsSummaryResponse.description:
`GET /comments/posts/insights/summary` — aggregate insights totals.

Totals across the tenant's comment-synced posts, for two windows. The
30-day window sums posts published (``posted_at``) in the last 30 days; the
all-time window sums every non-deleted post. Because per-post insights are
Meta LIFETIME totals, the window selects WHICH posts are summed, not a daily
series.

post_count.title: Post Count
post_count.description: Posts in this window that have cached insights (``insights_refreshed_at`` set) and therefore contributed to the totals above.

SocialPostInsightsWindow.title: SocialPostInsightsWindow
SocialPostInsightsWindow.description:
Summed insights across a set of comment-synced posts (one time window).

Per-post insights are Meta LIFETIME totals, so a window filters WHICH posts
are summed, NOT a per-day series — the totals are lifetime numbers for the
posts in scope. Each metric sums only the non-null cached values (so a metric
a platform never exposes never distorts the total); a metric is null only
when NO post in scope has a value for it. ``post_count`` is how many posts
have cached insights and thus contributed.

items.title: Items
items.description: List of items for this page

page_name.title: Page Name
page_name.description: Display name of the connected Page / Instagram account this post belongs to — the post owner (your connected account, not the commenter). Falls back to a channel-type label when the channel has no set name.

page_avatar_url.title: Page Avatar Url
page_avatar_url.description: Profile-picture URL of the connected Page / Instagram account. Nullable — a Meta CDN URL that can expire, and null for channels connected before the avatar was captured.

thumbnail_url.title: Thumbnail Url
thumbnail_url.description: Card image for the post — a permanent URL on our own domain when the image was mirrored, Meta's expiring CDN URL otherwise.

posted_at.title: Posted At
posted_at.description: When the post was published on Meta.

like_count.title: Like Count
like_count.description: Meta's total reaction count on the post. Nullable — null until the post has been read from Meta.

comments_count.title: Comments Count
comments_count.description: Meta's total comment count on the post. Nullable. DISTINCT from the count of comment rows WE stored (see `SocialPostResponse`).

SocialPostRef.title: SocialPostRef
SocialPostRef.description:
Compact post reference embedded in a comment row.

Present on the cross-post inbox and on a single comment, where the reader
has no post context; omitted from the per-post thread, where it would repeat
on every row.

updated_at.title: Updated At
updated_at.description: When the resource was last updated (UTC)

channel_id.title: Channel Id
channel_id.description: The Instagram or Facebook Messenger channel this post belongs to.

page_name.title: Page Name
page_name.description: Display name of the connected Page / Instagram account this post belongs to — the **post owner**, i.e. YOUR connected account, not the commenter. Taken from the channel's name, falling back to a channel-type label ("Instagram" / "Facebook Page") when the channel has no set name.

page_avatar_url.title: Page Avatar Url
page_avatar_url.description: Profile-picture URL of the connected Page / Instagram account (the post owner). **Nullable** — a Meta CDN URL that can expire, and null for channels connected before the avatar was captured or when Meta returned none. Fall back to initials/`page_name` when absent.

external_post_id.title: External Post Id
external_post_id.description: Meta's post id — an Instagram media id, or a Facebook `{page_id}_{post_id}`.

permalink.title: Permalink
permalink.description: Public URL of the post on Instagram / Facebook.

media_type.title: Media Type
media_type.description: Meta's media type — `image`, `video`, `carousel_album`, `reel`, `story`, `link`, … Not an enum: Meta adds new ones.

media_url.title: Media Url
media_url.description: Meta CDN URL of the media. **These URLs expire** — treat them as a cache, not as a durable reference, and fall back to `permalink`.

thumbnail_url.title: Thumbnail Url
thumbnail_url.description: URL of the post's card image. Normally a **permanent** URL on our own domain: we mirror the image once, because Meta's own CDN URLs expire. Falls back to Meta's expiring CDN URL for a post whose image could not be mirrored (it had already expired, or the post has no image at all).

posted_at.title: Posted At
posted_at.description: When the post was published on Meta — not when we learned about it. Null for a post Meta gave no timestamp for; such posts sort last.

like_count.title: Like Count
like_count.description: Total reactions Meta reports on the post (all reaction types on Facebook, likes on Instagram). **Nullable** — null until the post has been read from Meta, and it can lag reality between syncs. This is Meta's public number, not derived from anything we store.

comments_count.title: Comments Count
comments_count.description: Total comments Meta reports on the post. **Nullable** — null until read from Meta. DISTINCT from `comment_count`: `comment_count` is how many comments WE have stored (only those Meta delivered us), while `comments_count` is Meta's own total (includes nested replies and comments we were never sent), so the two legitimately differ.

comment_count.title: Comment Count
comment_count.description: Total comments we have stored for this post.

unanswered_count.title: Unanswered Count
unanswered_count.description: Comments still in `pending` — the badge the Comments UI shows. Advisory UI decoration maintained incrementally on ingestion and recomputed whenever a comment is triaged or purged; never used for billing.

counters_synced_at.title: Counters Synced At
counters_synced_at.description: Last time the two counters were recomputed from the comment rows. Null means they have only ever been maintained incrementally.

insights.description: Cached Meta insights for this post (reach, impressions, engagement, likes, comments, shares, saves, video_views, clicks) plus the authorization / freshness envelope. Served from the cache columns — NEVER a live Graph call on list load. Use `POST /comments/posts/{post_id}/insights/refresh` to force a fresh read. Null only for a post whose channel type carries no insights.

SocialPostResponse.title: SocialPostResponse
SocialPostResponse.description: One Instagram media / Facebook Page post we have comments for.

SourceType.title: SourceType
SourceType.description: Source type indicating which table the connection came from

contact_id.title: Contact Id
contact_id.description: Contact UUID on the tenant's shard

idempotency_key.title: Idempotency Key
idempotency_key.description: Optional caller-supplied idempotency key for at-most-once start semantics. If a run with the same (tenant_id, idempotency_key) already exists, the existing run is returned with HTTP 200 instead of creating a new one. If omitted, the engine derives a key from the request payload (e.g. ``manual:<flow_id>:<contact_id>:<request_id>``).

context.title: Context
context.description: Extra variables to seed ``flow_runs.context.vars``. Hard-capped at 16 KB JSON-encoded.

contact_method_overrides.title: Contact Method Overrides
contact_method_overrides.description: Optional map of ``ChannelType`` (string value, e.g. ``email``, ``sms``, ``whatsapp``, ``telegram``, ``messenger``, ``instagram``, ``browser_push``) → ``contact_method.id``. When the flow sends on the matching channel, this specific contact_method's value is used as the destination instead of the contact's primary method. Per-channel keys are independent; omitted channels fall back to the default (primary) resolution. Each referenced contact_method must belong to the same tenant, the same contact, and have a method_type that matches the channel key.

status.description: Subscription status (subscribed, pending, unsubscribed, bounced, complained)

count.title: Count

StatusCount.description: Count for a single subscription status

by_channel.description: Breakdown by channel type and status

period_start.description: Start of the reporting period (ISO format)

SubscriberOverviewResponse.description:
Subscriber overview with counts by status, channel, and list.

Returned by GET /api/v1/analytics/subscribers/overview

SubscriberTrendsResponse.description:
Subscriber growth trends over time.

Returned by GET /api/v1/analytics/subscribers/trends

SubscriptionActivityItem.description: A single opt-in or opt-out event derived from a subscription's current state.

SubscriptionChannelType.title: SubscriptionChannelType
SubscriptionChannelType.description: Channels a contact can hold a list subscription on.

channel_id.description: Channel ID (required for telegram, messenger, instagram)

opt_in_widget_id.title: Opt In Widget Id
opt_in_widget_id.description: Widget ID if subscribed via widget

SubscriptionStatsResponse.description: Schema for subscription statistics by list

SuccessResponse.title: SuccessResponse
SuccessResponse.description:
Standard success response for operations without data return.

Use for: DELETE operations, bulk updates, toggles, etc.

ai_answer_event_id.title: Ai Answer Event Id
ai_answer_event_id.description: AI answer event marked as accepted, if one was resolved

SuggestionAcceptResponse.title: SuggestionAcceptResponse
SuggestionAcceptResponse.description: Response when marking a suggestion as accepted.

type.title: Type
type.description: Source type: faq, article, ticket, manual

ticket_id.title: Ticket Id
ticket_id.description: Ticket ID if type is ticket

tags.title: Tags
tags.description: Associated tags

SuggestionSource.title: SuggestionSource
SuggestionSource.description: A source document used in generating the suggestion.

human_messages.title: Human Messages
human_messages.description: Human/manual agent-sent messages in the period (rollup-sourced)

SupportBreakdown.title: SupportBreakdown
SupportBreakdown.description:
Customer-support message volume in the period.

NOTE: `bot_messages` / `human_messages` are ROLLUP-SOURCED from the
interaction-log hourly rollup (TenantHourlyStats), NOT the billed-messages
table -- an explicit product decision. They are not invoice-exact.

WhatsAppTemplateComponent.title: WhatsAppTemplateComponent
WhatsAppTemplateComponent.description:
Component for WhatsApp template (header, body, button).

For button components Meta requires both ``sub_type``
(``url`` / ``quick_reply`` / ``flow`` / ``copy_code`` / ``voice_call`` / ``catalog``)
and ``index`` (``"0"`` / ``"1"`` / ``"2"``) on the send payload — see
https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/cloud-api/guides/send-message-templates#sending-buttons
Without them Meta returns ``(#100) Invalid parameter — button: Missing
parameter sub_type for button component`` (Sentry BACKEND-92).

Header / body components leave both fields ``None`` and are unaffected.

WhatsAppWindowStatusResponse.title: WhatsAppWindowStatusResponse
WhatsAppWindowStatusResponse.description:
Response for WhatsApp messaging window status check.

Two window kinds are represented:

- ``customer_service`` (default): standard 24-hour window measured from the
  last inbound customer message. Once expired, only template messages may
  be sent (``requires_template`` true).
- ``free_entry_point``: a 72-hour Free Entry Point (FEP) window for
  Click-to-WhatsApp / Page-CTA conversations. While open, ANY message type
  (free-form OR template) is allowed and is free of Meta charge.

Body of ``PUT /widgets/{widget_id}/identity-verification``.

body is normalised to ``{}`` so Pydantic never raises its own 422 (whose
body would echo the input); the endpoint returns its own 422
